citations.quote: The gallery is the only path by which fuel from one side reaches an engine on the other

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the gallery as the only inter-side fuel path and a recorded particular-risk item, but does not resolve its internal failure modes.

assumptions.text: The directional-control-shortfall branch of SF-001-PL2 is left undeveloped here because its contributors belong to the FCS/yaw architecture, not propulsion.
assumptions.ifWrong: If yaw contributors should be developed in this tree, the AND gate's right branch expands into rudder-segment/hydraulic-supply basic events, deepening the tree.

citations.quote: a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the asymmetric-thrust sizing case and split-rudder arrangement but does not resolve yaw-authority contributors within the propulsion description.

assumptions.text: The 3-way FCC vote/comparator provides monitoring coverage that must fail concurrently with a single FCC error for an erroneous or uncommanded command to reach the surfaces.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the vote does not isolate a single bad output, the FCC contributor becomes an order-1 (single-point) input under the OR gate rather than an AND, changing the tree structure and single-point-failure flag.
assumptions.usedFor: AND gates under SF-004-M and SF-004-M2

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the computers vote on command but does not describe the monitor's detection coverage, forcing an AND between a bad FCC output and a monitor non-detection.

assumptions.text: The three flight control computers are independent (separate bays, separate electrical sources) so a single common cause does not defeat the vote.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common cause defeats the vote, the FCC AND gate collapses toward a single point and the trees for both conditions must add a common-cause basic event.
assumptions.usedFor: FCC AND-gate inputs under SF-004-M and SF-004-M2

citations.quote: Each computer is supplied from a different electrical source

assumptions.rationale: Independence is claimed by installation in three separate bays and supply from three different electrical sources, but common-cause has not been assessed here.

assumptions.text: FCC and ACE internal architecture is the resolution limit; no deeper basic events are modelled because the SDD does not resolve their internals.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a lower-level FCC/ACE architecture is later provided, the corresponding basic events split into sub-trees.
assumptions.usedFor: Leaf basic events for FCC and ACE in both trees

citations.quote: electrical power to the computers and to the actuator control electronics

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes FCCs and actuator control electronics as blocks without sub-structure, so decomposing further would fabricate depth.

assumptions.text: A stabiliser trim runaway is arrested by a monitor/automatic cutout or crew action that is a distinct contributor from the erroneous drive itself.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-004-M3 trim-runaway branch AND gate collapses toward a single-event OR, changing the tree structure and any SPF finding.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M3 gate 'Stabiliser trim runaway to extreme' and its 'Failure to detect and arrest trim runaway' input

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim but does not state any trim-runaway monitoring or cutout logic, so the arrest mechanism is assumed rather than read.

assumptions.text: The three dissimilar FCCs form an independent command contributor to elevator loss such that all three command paths must be lost for elevator command loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single FCC or shared actuator-control-electronics feeds the elevators, the FCC branch becomes a lower-order cut set and SF-004-TL may expose a nearer single/dual point of failure.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL gate 'Loss of FCC command to elevator actuators'

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command. Each computer is supplied from a different electrical source

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three dissimilar computers on three separate electrical sources but does not confirm that every elevator actuator control path draws on all three, so the AND across FCC 1/2/3 is inferred.

assumptions.text: Elevators are driven by hydraulic systems A and C only, so loss of both A and C removes powered elevator authority.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an additional supply or a shared A/C dependency exists, the elevator-loss AND gate order changes and the independence claim in SF-004-TL is affected.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL gate 'Loss of elevator control' A and C branches; SF-004-M3 elevator actuator inputs

citations.quote: the elevators from A and C; the ailerons from B and C

assumptions.rationale: The SDD assigns 'the elevators from A and C'; the tree's dual-supply AND for elevator loss rests directly on that allocation.

assumptions.text: The upper rudder segment is supplied by HYD A and the lower segment by HYD B.
assumptions.ifWrong: The specific hydraulic-loss basic events under each SF-005-TL segment branch swap systems; gate logic (AND of two segments) is unchanged.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL nodes 'Loss of HYD A supply to upper rudder' and 'Loss of HYD B supply to lower rudder'

citations.quote: A → rudder upper, elevators; B → rudder lower, ailerons

assumptions.rationale: §5.3.2 states each segment has its own hydraulic supply but the A/B-to-segment mapping is only given in the §2.2 interface line 'A → rudder upper, elevators; B → rudder lower, ailerons'.

assumptions.text: The mechanical reversion path backs up only the lower rudder segment, so upper-segment command loss has no mechanical backstop.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversion also serves the upper segment, the upper command-loss branch becomes an AND (FBW + reversion) rather than a single OR input.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL asymmetry between upper (OR command) and lower (AND command) branches

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: §5.3.2 states the mechanical reversion path exists 'to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only'.

assumptions.text: 'Below detection threshold' for SF-006-M3 means the asymmetry-detection and asymmetry-brake protection must also fail (or not act) for the condition to exist.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the detection layer is not credited, the top event reduces to an OR of the asymmetry mechanisms alone and the protective AND branch is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006-M3 top AND gate and its 'protection fails to detect/arrest' branch

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.rationale: The FC is defined as below the detection threshold; the SDD provides asymmetry brakes and asymmetry/jam discretes as the protection, so the undetected condition requires that protection to fail to arrest/annunciate.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of ground support at touchdown is dominated by failure to reach a locked-down gear configuration and by gear structural collapse, with no other credible top contributor.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a third independent contributor exists (e.g. bogie tyre/flotation failure driving loss of support), the SF-007-TL OR gate gains a branch.

citations.quote: One twin-wheel steerable nose unit and six three-wheel main bogies, three per side

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes extension/lockdown and treats gear structure as non-redundant, but does not enumerate touchdown-load failure modes, forcing a two-branch model.

assumptions.text: The free-fall alternate extension is genuinely independent of HYD system A, so both must fail for gear not to reach lockdown.
assumptions.ifWrong: If free-fall shares a failure source with HYD-A extension, the AND collapses toward a single-point path and SF-007-TL loses its independence claim.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-007-TL 'Gear not in locked-down configuration' AND gate

citations.quote: free-fall extension independent of hydraulic pressure

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states free-fall is an alternate to HYD-A extension but does not detail its actuation independence.

assumptions.text: The two dissimilar lock-sensing channels are independent, so a false 'locked' indication requires BOTH channels to fail false while pins are not driven.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common cause defeats both channels, the SF-010-M sensing AND collapses to an OR and the condition becomes near single-point.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-M 'Both dissimilar sensing channels falsely indicate locked' AND gate

citations.quote: a proximity sensing harness reading pin position directly, and a mechanical linkage driving a visual indicator

assumptions.rationale: The SDD claims dissimilar and independently routed sensing but this independence is asserted, not substantiated.

assumptions.text: The pin actuator and its separate hydraulic supply resolve no deeper than actuator/supply-level basic events for this pass.
assumptions.ifWrong: If piece-part resolution is required, the pins-not-driven OR branch expands with additional basic events.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-M 'Locking pins not driven' OR gate

citations.quote: Eight independent locking pins are then driven through the latch bodies by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply but does not decompose its internal fault modes.

assumptions.text: The common torque shaft driving all twelve latches is a single element whose failure defeats the entire latch set.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the torque shaft is segmented/redundant, the 'Common torque shaft failure' order-1 event should be replaced by an AND across segments, changing the latch branch structure.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-TL latch-set OR branch, basic event 'Common torque shaft failure (all twelve latches)'

citations.quote: Twelve rotary latches engage on closure, driven by a common torque shaft.

assumptions.rationale: SDD states the twelve rotary latches are 'driven by a common torque shaft' but does not decompose the shaft into segments or state any redundancy in it.

assumptions.text: The locking pins are engaged by a single lock actuator on a single (separate) hydraulic supply, distinct from the latch drive.
assumptions.ifWrong: If pin actuation is redundant, the pin OR branch understates margin; if the pin supply shares a source with the latch drive, the engagement AND collapses toward order-1.

citations.quote: Eight independent locking pins are then driven through the latch bodies by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply

assumptions.rationale: SDD says eight pins are 'driven through the latch bodies by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply' but does not state whether the pin actuator itself is redundant.

assumptions.text: Loss of longitudinal restraint at one station requires loss of BOTH straps at that station OR loss of the station's single saddle-to-hardpoint load path.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single strap loss alone constitutes 'loss of longitudinal restraint at one station' the top gate becomes an OR of single straps, making each strap an order-1 cut set.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-PL top-gate structure and both-strap AND

citations.quote: load paths sized such that the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours. There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points

assumptions.rationale: SDD gives two straps per saddle and states 'no redundancy in the hold floor hard points'; the FC is single-station loss so both-strap failure plus the shared hardpoint are the contributors.

assumptions.text: The two lock-confirmation channels (proximity harness and mechanical linkage/indicator) are independent and both must fail for confirmation to be lost.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the two channels share a route or penetration, the confirmation AND becomes a common-cause candidate and the branch weakens toward order-1.

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.rationale: SDD describes the two circuits as 'dissimilar and independently routed'; independence is asserted in the design and must be verified, not assumed.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of restraint requires either failure of the shared hold-floor hard-point load path or simultaneous loss of both straps and saddle geometry at effectively every station.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a smaller subset of stations can produce complete restraint loss, the AND across all nine stations is too conservative and the tree should broaden to an OR over fewer-station combinations.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-TL top-event OR gate and the all-stations AND sub-gate

citations.quote: There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes redundancy such that one strap loss is carried by neighbours, so a whole-payload restraint loss is only reached by the common attachment path or a near-total strap/geometry loss; the SDD does not enumerate the failure condition itself.

assumptions.text: The hold-floor hard points / saddle attachment constitute a single non-redundant load path that is itself a potential single point of failure (order-1 cut set).
assumptions.ifWrong: If treated purely as structure substantiated outside the functional tree, this branch is removed from the FTA and handled via structural/particular-risk analysis instead.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-TL top-event OR-gate first input (hard-point basic event)

citations.quote: Saddles are pinned to hard points in the hold floor beam structure.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states no redundancy in the hard points; whether this qualifies as structure (substantiated by structural analysis/PRA) rather than a functional basic event needs engineering disposition.

assumptions.text: The restraint tension monitoring loop is indication only and does not itself provide or restore restraint, so it is not a contributor to loss of restraint.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loss of monitoring is deemed to defeat a credited crew mitigation, a monitor/detection branch (inhibit gate) would need adding.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of the tension-loop branch from SF-012-TL

citations.quote: In flight the crew has indication only; there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states in-flight the crew has indication only with no in-flight adjustment of restraint; the loop is a monitor, not a restraint element.

assumptions.text: Only the two inboard engines carry reversers, so SF-002-M is an OR over exactly two inboard reverser units and outboards contribute nothing.
assumptions.ifWrong: The OR would gain or lose reverser-unit branches, changing the cut-set structure.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-M top-level OR (two inboard reverser branches)

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only; the tree must not include outboard units.

assumptions.text: The WOW/RA in-flight inhibit and the mechanical translating-sleeve lock are independent of each other and of the deploy-command source, so their common failure is not order-1.
assumptions.ifWrong: A shared cause would collapse the AND to an order-1/order-2 cut set, unacceptable for a Catastrophic condition.

citations.quote: inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists both inhibits but does not substantiate their mutual independence or their independence from the command path.

assumptions.text: Roll spoilers are commanded by the same three FCCs and multi-function; complete roll loss therefore requires both aileron AND spoiler roll authority to be lost (AND at top).
assumptions.ifWrong: If spoilers give no usable roll authority, the top AND collapses and roll loss reduces to the aileron sub-tree alone.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-TL top-level AND (aileron AND spoiler branches)

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names ailerons and multi-function spoilers as the roll effectors but does not detail spoiler hydraulic supply or FCC channel assignment.

assumptions.text: Aileron actuation is a two-supply set (HYD B and HYD C) and three dissimilar FCC command paths; HYD B and HYD C are independent at the aileron actuators.
assumptions.ifWrong: If B and C share a cause at the ailerons, the hydraulic AND becomes an effective single point, unacceptable for Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-TL aileron hydraulic AND and FCC-command AND gates

citations.quote: the ailerons from B and C.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD assigns ailerons to HYD B and C and to three FCCs but does not confirm B/C are free of common-mode at the aileron actuators.

assumptions.text: There is no mechanical reversion to the roll axis, so roll authority cannot be recovered by a mechanical path after loss of electrical/hydraulic drive.
assumptions.ifWrong: A roll reversion path would add an AND term and prevent complete roll loss from the modelled contributors.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-TL (absence of a mechanical-reversion recovery branch)

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states reversion exists only to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder segment, implying none for roll.

assumptions.text: An uncommanded thrust change on any single engine, alone, satisfies the SF-001-M top event.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the condition were intended only for a common uncommanded change across engines, the top gate would become AND / a common-cause structure and the single-engine branches would drop out.
assumptions.usedFor: Top OR gate of SF-001-M and the four per-engine OR branches

citations.quote: Uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines with no crew command

assumptions.rationale: The failure condition text says 'one or more engines', so the tree must be an OR across engines rather than requiring multiple engines to fail together.

assumptions.text: An uncommanded (not merely lost) thrust command from the FADEC requires both dual-redundant channels to produce the erroneous command, so the FADEC-originated branch is an AND of the two channels.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single channel can drive an uncommanded thrust change without the other agreeing, each FADEC branch becomes a single-point OR contributor rather than an AND, weakening the qualitative margin for this Hazardous condition.
assumptions.usedFor: The 'FADEC-originated uncommanded thrust command (both channels)' AND gate on each of engines 1–4

citations.quote: digital engine control with dual redundant channels and independent power feeds, cross-linked to the opposite channel for data only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dual redundant channels cross-linked for data; it does not state the channel voting/comparator logic, so the AND depth for an active erroneous output is an assumption pending the FADEC control law.

assumptions.text: Each engine's uncommanded thrust change is independent of the others because engine services and FADEC power sources are segregated per engine.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a shared resource can drive a correlated uncommanded change across engines, a common-cause branch must be added under the top OR and the independence claim in any allocation is invalid.
assumptions.usedFor: The four independent per-engine OR branches of SF-001-M

citations.quote: arranged so that no single bus loss can affect more than one engine

assumptions.rationale: The SDD claims per-engine segregation and four different FADEC power sources, but the interface matrix shows a shared cross-feed fuel gallery and a shared bleed manifold that could be common-cause paths not developed in this functional tree.

assumptions.text: A single main-gear tyre burst can liberate debris reaching both the separately-clipped HYD A and HYD B brake bundles sharing the same gear bay.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the bundles as co-located but 'separately clipped and shielded' without stating the debris trajectory or clip separation distance, so I cannot conclude the independence holds.
assumptions.ifWrong: If separation is shown adequate against the burst trajectory, the CSFL against SF-008 braking is void and no common-cause contributor is added to the SF-008 trees.
assumptions.usedFor: Tire Burst PRA row csfl and requirement candidates; SF-008 linkage.

citations.quote: separately clipped and shielded but sharing the bay

assumptions.text: A single bird-strike impact field on the forward fuselage can encompass both same-type ice detectors and/or multiple air-data probes.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives 'opposite sides of the forward fuselage' but no lateral separation dimension against a defined bird-strike envelope, so common-envelope loss cannot be excluded.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detector/probe separation exceeds the impact envelope, the ice-detection and air-data common-cause candidates against SF-017/SF-018 are void.
assumptions.usedFor: Bird Strike PRA row csfl and requirement candidates; SF-017/SF-018 linkage.

citations.quote: Two ice detectors of the same type are installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage

assumptions.text: The bird-strike energy/altitude envelope is the standard Part 25 type-design bird envelope pending refinement.
assumptions.rationale: The applicability note directs refinement to the type-design bird envelope but no envelope value is provided in the inputs.
assumptions.ifWrong: A larger envelope would broaden the affected zones and could change which failure conditions are credibly caused.
assumptions.usedFor: Bird Strike PRA row desc and severity framing.

citations.quote: for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis

assumptions.text: The three flight control computers' dissimilarity (different sources, two software teams) provides genuine common-mode immunity to lightning-induced transients and HIRF, not merely random-fault independence.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts dissimilarity as a design claim but provides no lightning/HIRF qualification evidence; App A explicitly says independence claims must be tested rather than assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: The lightning and HIRF CSFL entries escalate to a credible common-cause loss of all three FCC command paths, driving SF-004-TL/SF-005-TL/SF-003 toward simultaneous loss and requiring the mechanical reversion path to be the sole survivability claim.
assumptions.usedFor: CSFL field of both Lightning and HIRF PRA rows; the FCC-related requirement candidates

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command. Each computer is supplied from a different electrical source

assumptions.text: The mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and lower rudder is genuinely independent of any electrical/electronic path and therefore survives a lightning/HIRF event that takes all three FCCs.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states reversion results from loss of all electrical command paths, but does not confirm the reversion mechanism itself carries no electrically-vulnerable element susceptible to the same transient/field.
assumptions.ifWrong: The 'mechanical reversion' mitigation cited for the Lightning row is void, removing the last survivability claim for pitch/yaw control under a common-mode electromagnetic event.
assumptions.usedFor: mitigation field of the Lightning PRA row

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: The two HV/LV route crossing points in zone 300, where physical separation is replaced by shielding, do not become a coupling site that defeats the left/right redundancy under lightning transients.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD flags these crossing points as installation items to be examined but gives no transient-isolation substantiation; final clamping/bundle build is not frozen.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Lightning CSFL is strengthened — the crossing points become a single location that couples both routes, and a dedicated CMA/ZSA finding plus a fault-tree common-cause contributor in the affected trees would be required.
assumptions.usedFor: csfl and requirements fields of the Lightning PRA row

citations.quote: two identified crossing points in the mid equipment bay where physical separation is replaced by shielding

assumptions.text: The Aeolus HL-1 is certificated for flight in the icing envelope of its certification basis, making ice accretion a credible in-service PRA threat.
assumptions.rationale: The applicability list marks Ice APPLICABLE but the SDD only states IPS exists 'for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis' without confirming the aircraft is dispatched into icing.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the aircraft is restricted from known icing, the Ice PRA row narrows to inadvertent-encounter survivability and several failure-condition links drop.
assumptions.usedFor: Ice PRA row and its SF-016/SF-017 function links

citations.quote: for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis

assumptions.text: Bleed anti-ice to wings and inlets shares the single cross-bleed manifold as a common source, so its loss is a common-cause across wing and inlet ice protection.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states wing and cowl bleed protection is taken from the same manifold that supplies the ECS packs, but does not state whether manifold isolation preserves anti-ice independence.
assumptions.ifWrong: If manifold isolation preserves per-side independence, the CSFL claim in the Ice row is removed and SF-016-TL is not a manifold common-cause.
assumptions.usedFor: Ice PRA row csfl field and the cross-bleed-manifold requirement candidate

citations.quote: taken from the same manifold that supplies the environmental packs, through piccolo distribution

assumptions.text: A single credible hail encounter can strike more than one engine inlet simultaneously, creating a common-cause across the propulsion thrust branches.
assumptions.rationale: The four engines are podded across a 160 m span; the SDD gives geometry but no hail-cone/simultaneity data to bound how many inlets a single encounter strikes.
assumptions.ifWrong: If only one inlet can be struck per encounter, the Hail row's propulsion CSFL is downgraded to a single-engine effect and the multi-engine inlet requirement candidate is unnecessary.
assumptions.usedFor: Hail PRA row csfl field and the engine-inlet hail requirement candidate

citations.quote: Engines are numbered 1 to 4 from left outboard to right outboard

assumptions.text: The hold fire load in flight is limited to the blade and non-combustible saddle/restraint hardware, with no combustible palletised load.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts a blade-only payload but does not characterise the actual fire load (blade material combustibility, strap/winch materials), which is needed to judge whether the no-suppression decision is acceptable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the blade or restraint materials present a meaningful in-flight fire load, the no-suppression decision fails §25.855 substantiation and a suppression requirement would be raised.
assumptions.usedFor: Cabin/hold fire PRA row — mitigation and no-suppression substantiation requirement

citations.quote: the hold carries a single blade and no combustible palletised load

assumptions.text: A single fire event in zone 300 can reach both FCC 2 and the HV/LV crossing points before detection and crew response arrest it.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD locates FCC 2 and the HV/LV crossing points both in zone 300 but does not state their internal separation within the zone, so common-cause potential cannot be confirmed or excluded from the document alone.
assumptions.ifWrong: If FCC 2 and the crossing points are adequately separated or fire-protected within zone 300, the CSFL claim is removed and no common-cause contributor is added to the FCS trees.
assumptions.usedFor: Cabin/hold fire PRA row — csfl field and the FCS common-cause requirement

citations.quote: Mid hold (stations 4–6) Saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points

assumptions.text: No fixed fire suppression is fitted in the forward equipment bay (zone 120) or flight deck (zone 130); only portable extinguishers are available forward.
assumptions.rationale: The FPR description lists fixed detection/suppression only for engine, APU, bleed-duct, gear-bay and hold zones; it does not describe forward-bay suppression, so its absence is inferred rather than stated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If forward-bay fixed suppression exists, the equipment-bay fire row mitigation understates the protection and the associated requirement is unnecessary.
assumptions.usedFor: Forward equipment bay / flight-deck fire PRA row — mitigation and requirements

citations.quote: Portable extinguishers are provided at the flight deck and at the hold access door

assumptions.text: The eighteen zones and their principal contents in SDD §3 are the authoritative zoning scheme to analyze against.
assumptions.rationale: No separate zonal model exists in CURRENT PROJECT STATE (zsa count is 0); the SDD zonal breakdown is the only supplied zone definition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the zone list or contents change, the housed-equipment and functional-impact fields for the affected zones change.

citations.quote: Eighteen zones per §3, with the zone-spanning routings of §4 drawn over the airframe.

assumptions.text: HYD systems A and B sharing the wing-root run through zones 530/300/540 is a genuine common-cause coupling that must be reflected in the affected fault trees.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD flags the shared run as a 'recorded installation item' to be examined but does not resolve whether it defeats independence; ARP4761A requires testing every AND-gate independence claim.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the run is proven fully separated at build, the CMA-candidate flag and the zone 530/300/540 interference finding downgrade to a closed observation.

citations.quote: Systems A and B nonetheless share a wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary

assumptions.text: Brake hydraulic lines A and B sharing each main gear bay (710/720) is a common-cause candidate for the wheel-braking fault trees.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the co-location as a zonal item; separately-clipped bundles do not by themselves defeat a single-bay event (tyre burst, fire) taking both.
assumptions.ifWrong: If separation is substantiated as adequate against the bay threats, the braking-tree common-cause contributor is removed.

citations.quote: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through each main gear bay in adjacent bundles

assumptions.text: The hold's smoke-detection-without-suppression decision (zones 200/300/400) is an open item requiring substantiation, not a closed design.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly carries it forward as an assumption to be substantiated; it is not yet a compliant baseline.
assumptions.ifWrong: If suppression is later required, the hold zones gain equipment and the fire-related functional impact changes.

citations.quote: hold suppression is deliberately not fitted. That decision is recorded and carried forward as an assumption to be substantiated

assumptions.text: The outboard engines (zones 610/640) at the 28 m moment arm generate a rotor-burst debris trajectory that bears on wing structure and opposite-side runs.
assumptions.rationale: The applicable-risk set mandates rotor burst; the debris trajectory relative to zonal contents is inferred from the stated moment arm, not drawn in the SDD.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the debris trajectory does not intersect the claimed runs, the 610/640 inter-zone interference finding narrows.
assumptions.usedFor: Interference field for zones 610, 640; bearing rotor-burst PRA cross-link

citations.quote: The outboard engine moment arm is 28 m, taken as 0.35 of the 80 m semi-span

assumptions.text: Fault-tree node id 1 (top AND on the 'Complete loss of propulsive thrust' page) is the gate labelled G-006.
assumptions.rationale: The turn references gates by G-labels but the project state exposes numeric node ids; I mapped by top-event name.
assumptions.ifWrong: The link action for G-006 targets the wrong gate and must be re-pointed to the correct node id.

citations.quote: one 105 m blade of up to 72.6 t occupying the full hold length

assumptions.text: Node id 21 (top AND on the asymmetric-thrust page) is gate G-008 and node 27 (FCC erroneous-command AND) is gate G-009.
assumptions.rationale: Same G-label to numeric-id mapping gap; matched by top-event/gate name.
assumptions.ifWrong: The G-008/G-009 links target wrong gates and must be re-pointed.
