praData.threat: Tire burst / flailing tread release (§25.734 / AC 25.734-1) — 20-tyre gear, six three-wheel main bogies plus twin-wheel nose unit; debris and tread liberated radially and tangentially at burst.
praData.desc: A main-gear tyre burst in zone 710 or 720 liberates casing fragments and flailing tread within the main gear bay, which houses three bogies per side plus the system A and B brake hydraulic lines and the steering and brake harnesses. A nose-gear tyre burst is confined to zone 730 (nose unit, steering actuator, tow disconnect). The main gear bays carry brake lines A and B in 'adjacent but separately clipped bundles' sharing the bay — a recorded zonal item — so a single burst is a credible common-cause candidate against both brake supplies co-located in that bay. Installation evidence is at drawing/model stage (Fig 6-1); tread trajectory into the bundles is not established.
praData.systems: LDG (Landing Gear & Braking); HYD systems A and B where their brake lines transit the gear bays; FCS insofar as HYD A/B brake-line loss is bay-local only.
praData.csfl: Co-location of HYD A (alternate braking) and HYD B (normal braking) brake lines in the same main gear bay is a candidate common source that could defeat the dual-hydraulic braking independence claimed in SDD §5.6.2. Debris reaching both separately-clipped bundles would be the common cause; if realised it must be carried into the SF-008 (wheel braking) fault trees as a common-cause contributor rather than left out because the logical redundancy looks adequate.
praData.mitigation:
Brake lines A and B run in adjacent but separately clipped and shielded bundles within each bay (SDD §5.6.5); steering and braking electrical harnesses routed on opposite sides of each bay; accumulator-supported emergency braking sized to six full applications with all three hydraulic systems lost (§5.4.3); free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure. Acceptability CLAIM: MINIMISED for braking degradation via accumulator reserve and the 1,080 m rollout vs 1,800 m requirement margin — SHOWN-TO-BE-ACCEPTABLE is NOT yet established for simultaneous loss of both A and B brake supplies to a bay and requires debris-trajectory substantiation.
Proposed requirements: • Separation/shielding of HYD A and HYD B brake-line bundles within each main gear bay shall be substantiated against the tyre-burst debris trajectory such that a single burst cannot sever both bundles.
• Anti-skid and brake-control harness routing shall be shown segregated from the tyre-burst debris field within zones 710/720.
aiRequirements: Separation/shielding of HYD A and HYD B brake-line bundles within each main gear bay shall be substantiated against the tyre-burst debris trajectory such that a single burst cannot sever both bundles.
Anti-skid and brake-control harness routing shall be shown segregated from the tyre-burst debris field within zones 710/720.

praData.threat: Bird strike (§25.571(e)(1) / §25.631 / §33.76) — external impact on forward-facing structures, engine inlets, probes and windshields; to be refined to the type-design bird envelope.
praData.desc: A bird strike impacts forward-facing surfaces: the four podded engine inlets (zones 610-640) with potential ingestion, the wing leading edges (zones 510/520) and their piccolo anti-ice ducting, and the flight-deck windshields and forward-mounted probes/ice detectors (two ice detectors on opposite sides of the forward fuselage; probes and static ports; windshields serving zone 130). Two ice detectors are of the same type — a commonality recorded for examination — raising a single-strike-envelope concern if both forward-fuselage detectors sit in a common impact field. Ingestion into an engine may cause thrust loss or, at worst, rotor/fan damage (assessed separately under the engine/rotor-burst risks in other turns).
praData.systems: PRP (engine inlets, four separate nacelle zones — left/right pairs in separate zones); AVI (probes, static ports, windshields, ice detectors); IPS (ice detectors, wing leading-edge anti-ice); FCS insofar as air-data/AOA sensing feeds command.
praData.csfl: The two ice detectors are 'identical in type' and mounted on opposite sides of the forward fuselage (SDD §5.10.2); a strike envelope large enough to take both is a candidate common source against ice-detection availability. Loss/erroneous output of multiple co-located forward air-data probes from a single strike is a candidate common cause against the air-data feed to FCS and displays and must be reflected in the SF-017 / SF-018 fault trees if realised.
praData.mitigation:
Engines numbered 1-4 with left and right pairs in separate zones; services to each engine routed through the corresponding pylon and not commingled with the opposite side outboard of the wing root (§5.1.5), so a single strike cannot take engines on both sides. Three air-data inertial reference units, one on the DC essential bus; independent integrated standby instrument sharing no sensor with the primaries (§5.11.2/§5.11.3). Two ice detectors on opposite sides of the forward fuselage. Acceptability CLAIM: MINIMISED for single-engine ingestion (continued flight after loss of any one engine per §5.1.3); windshield/structure survivability and probe/detector common-envelope loss are NOT yet SHOWN-TO-BE-ACCEPTABLE and require bird-impact substantiation to the type-design envelope.
Proposed requirements: • Windshield and forward-fuselage structure shall withstand bird impact to the type-design bird envelope without loss of flight-deck integrity or crew incapacitation.
• Forward air-data probe and ice-detector locations shall be shown separated such that a single bird-strike impact field cannot defeat the redundant air-data and ice-detection functions.
aiRequirements: Windshield and forward-fuselage structure shall withstand bird impact to the type-design bird envelope without loss of flight-deck integrity or crew incapacitation.
Forward air-data probe and ice-detector locations shall be shown separated such that a single bird-strike impact field cannot defeat the redundant air-data and ice-detection functions.

praData.threat: Lightning strike (§25.1316, AC 20-136B) — direct attachment and indirect effects coupling transients onto electrical/electronic wiring
praData.desc: Direct attachment zones are extremities and forward-facing/large-surface structure (wing leading edges 510/520, nacelles 610–640, empennage/aft fuselage 800, nose visor 110). Indirect effects couple transients onto the six EWS routes (HV feeder L/R through 610/620,530,300,200; LV signal L/R through 120,200,300,400,800; data channels 1&2). Effect assessment: aircraft survivability depends on the transients not simultaneously defeating the three dissimilar FCCs (installed in separate bays 120/300/400 on three sources) nor the DC-essential-fed standby instrument that shares no supply/sensor/processing with primaries. Development stage: drawing/model — final bundle build and clamping positions are not frozen, so separation is a candidate not a verified result.
praData.systems: FCS, EPS, AVI, IPS, FPR, ECS, PRP (FADEC), CRG (tension loop), NZD (lock sensing)
praData.csfl: Lightning-induced transients are a common cause across otherwise-independent FCC command paths (SF-004-TL complete loss of pitch, SF-005-TL complete loss of yaw, SF-003 loss of roll) if coupling defeats the FCC dissimilarity/segregation argument; also across the two HV/LV crossing points in zone 300 where physical separation is replaced by shielding.
praData.mitigation:
Structural bonding/diverter provisions on attachment zones; EWS separation of HV/LV routes with shielding at the two zone-300 crossing points; three dissimilar FCCs on three sources in three bays; mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and lower rudder independent of electrical command; standby instrument on DC essential sharing nothing with primaries; smoke detection at nine hold stations. Claim per App L: effects to be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE via §25.1316 transient control level substantiation — not yet demonstrated at this development stage.
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft electrical/electronic installation shall protect Level A flight-control and display functions against §25.1316 lightning-induced transients such that no single strike defeats the FCC dissimilarity and segregation argument.
• The two HV/LV route crossing points in zone 300 shall be substantiated to maintain lightning transient isolation between the crossing routes.
aiFunctions: SF-018 Acquire and present flight and navigation data
aiRequirements: The aircraft electrical/electronic installation shall protect Level A flight-control and display functions against §25.1316 lightning-induced transients such that no single strike defeats the FCC dissimilarity and segregation argument.
The two HV/LV route crossing points in zone 300 shall be substantiated to maintain lightning transient isolation between the crossing routes.

praData.threat: High-Intensity Radiated Fields (§25.1317, AC 20-158A) — external RF field coupling into electrical/electronic systems and wiring
praData.desc: HIRF illuminates the whole airframe; coupling is into apertures and along the six EWS routes rather than to one zone. The dual redundant deterministic data network (channels 1&2, opposite sides, no shared connector/penetration) and the three dissimilar FCCs are the fly-by-wire elements most exposed. Effect assessment: aircraft survivability depends on HIRF not simultaneously corrupting all three FCC command paths, the display processing chain, and the independent standby instrument. Development stage: drawing/model — routing definition preliminary, so aperture/shielding adequacy is a candidate not verified.
praData.systems: FCS, AVI, EPS, PRP (FADEC), FPR, ECS, IPS, CRG (tension monitoring), LDG (brake control/anti-skid electrical)
praData.csfl: HIRF is a common-mode threat across the three dissimilar FCCs (SF-003/004/005) and across the dual data network channels serving AVI (SF-018 erroneous/lost flight-nav data; SF-019 crew alerting) — corruption is common-cause even where the logical channels are independent, because the field couples into all channels at once.
praData.mitigation:
Airframe shielding/aperture control; dual data network on opposite sides sharing no connector or penetration; three dissimilar FCCs on three sources; standby instrument on DC essential independent of primary displays; FADEC dual channels on four different power sources cross-linked for data only. Claim per App L: effects to be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE via §25.1317 HIRF equipment/system qualification and installation test — not yet demonstrated at this development stage.
Proposed requirements: • Flight-control, display, alerting and engine-control functions shall meet §25.1317 HIRF susceptibility criteria at equipment and installed-system level such that HIRF does not simultaneously corrupt all redundant command/display channels.
• The dual data network installation shall be substantiated to maintain HIRF immunity across both channels without common-mode field coupling.
aiFunctions: SF-018 Acquire and present flight and navigation data
aiRequirements: Flight-control, display, alerting and engine-control functions shall meet §25.1317 HIRF susceptibility criteria at equipment and installed-system level such that HIRF does not simultaneously corrupt all redundant command/display channels.
The dual data network installation shall be substantiated to maintain HIRF immunity across both channels without common-mode field coupling.

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact (§25.571(e)(2)) — forward-facing hailstone impact on nose visor, wing leading edges, engine inlets and forward-fuselage ice detectors
praData.desc: Hailstone impact on forward-facing structure and inlets. Model each impact by size/energy against: the nose visor (110, a single-load-path pressure-boundary structure with no structural redundancy), wing leading edges (510/520/530/540) shared by wing anti-ice ducting and the outboard electrical route behind a shielded partition, the four engine inlets (610-640), and the two same-type ice detectors on opposite sides of the forward fuselage (120 region). Survivability question: does the aircraft continue after the credible hail encounter across all struck functions.
praData.systems: NZD, FCS (high-lift/leading edge), PRP (inlets), IPS (detectors, wing/cowl anti-ice), AVI (air-data probes forward of impact)
praData.csfl: Multiple engine inlets struck simultaneously by a single hail encounter is a common-cause across the otherwise-independent PRP thrust branches (page 'Complete loss of propulsive thrust' engine 1-4 legs); simultaneous impact on both forward-fuselage ice detectors of the same type defeats the IPS detection independence claim.
praData.mitigation:
Proposed requirements: • The nose visor structure shall withstand the certification hailstone impact without loss of pressure-boundary or forward structural load-path integrity (candidate — verify against §25.571(e)(2) / structural analysis + PRA).
• The engine inlet installation shall tolerate the certification hail encounter without simultaneous loss of thrust on more than the number of engines assumed in the propulsion FHA (candidate — verify against §25.901/903 and the thrust fault trees).
• Forward-facing air-data probes and both ice detectors shall be installed/shielded so a single hail encounter does not simultaneously disable redundant channels (candidate — addresses same-type ice-detector commonality).
aiFunctions: SF-016 Protect airframe and inlets from ice
SF-017 Heat probes and provide ice detection
SF-018 Acquire and present flight and navigation data
aiRequirements: The nose visor structure shall withstand the certification hailstone impact without loss of pressure-boundary or forward structural load-path integrity (candidate — verify against §25.571(e)(2) / structural analysis + PRA).

The engine inlet installation shall tolerate the certification hail encounter without simultaneous loss of thrust on more than the number of engines assumed in the propulsion FHA (candidate — verify against §25.901/903 and the thrust fault trees).

Forward-facing air-data probes and both ice detectors shall be installed/shielded so a single hail encounter does not simultaneously disable redundant channels (candidate — addresses same-type ice-detector commonality).

praData.threat: Icing / ice accretion and shedding (§25.1419, AC 20-73A) within the type-design ice envelope — accretion on unprotected/failed-protection surfaces, probes and inlets, and shed-ice impact
praData.desc: Model ice accretion on wing/cowl leading edges (510/520/530/540, bleed-fed anti-ice via cross-bleed manifold), engine inlets (610-640), the electrically heated stabiliser leading edges in the aft fuselage (800, six independently supplied zones), and heated probes/static ports/windshields/ice detectors (120/130 region). Model shed-ice trajectory into downstream inlets. Detection is provided by two ice detectors of the SAME type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage — a recorded commonality. Failure to activate protection when accretion exists, or undetected loss of protection to a surface/inlet zone, is the survivability driver.
praData.systems: IPS, PRP (inlets), ECS/PRP (cross-bleed manifold source), FCS (leading-edge/stabiliser aerodynamics), AVI (heated probes)
praData.csfl: Bleed anti-ice for wings and inlets is fed from the shared cross-bleed manifold in zone 300 — loss of that manifold is a common source across wing and inlet protection (SF-016-PL / SF-016-TL). The two ice detectors being identical in type is a common-mode that can defeat SF-017-M2 detection independence across both sides.
praData.mitigation:
Proposed requirements: • The cross-bleed manifold source common to wing and inlet anti-ice shall be assessed as a common-cause contributor in the ice-protection fault trees rather than treated as independent supply (candidate — reflects shared-manifold CSFL).
• The two ice detectors shall be assessed for same-type common-mode failure to annunciate accretion, and dissimilarity or independent monitoring provided if the FHA target for SF-017-M2 requires it (candidate).
• Ice-shedding trajectory from protected surfaces and inlets shall be shown not to cause unacceptable secondary damage to downstream engine inlets or control surfaces (candidate — §25.1419 / PRA).
aiFunctions: SF-016 Protect airframe and inlets from ice
SF-017 Heat probes and provide ice detection
SF-018 Acquire and present flight and navigation data
aiRequirements: The cross-bleed manifold source common to wing and inlet anti-ice shall be assessed as a common-cause contributor in the ice-protection fault trees rather than treated as independent supply (candidate — reflects shared-manifold CSFL).

The two ice detectors shall be assessed for same-type common-mode failure to annunciate accretion, and dissimilarity or independent monitoring provided if the FHA target for SF-017-M2 requires it (candidate).
Ice-shedding trajectory from protected surfaces and inlets shall be shown not to cause unacceptable secondary damage to downstream engine inlets or control surfaces (candidate — §25.1419 / PRA).

praData.threat: Cabin/hold fire — in-flight fire or overheat within the pressurised hold, detected but not suppressed
praData.desc: Hold carries smoke detection at nine stations and NO suppression (SDD §5.12.2). A fire originating in or reaching zones 200/300/400 has no active extinguishing means; the blade payload is the only intended content and no combustible palletised load is carried. Fire can reach equipment in the mid equipment bay (FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points, zone 300) and aft equipment bay (FCC 3, zone 400).
praData.systems: CRG, FPR, FCS (FCC 2 in zone 300, FCC 3 in zone 400), EWS
praData.csfl: A hold fire in zone 300 co-locates FCC 2 with the HV/LV crossing points and the HV feeder / LV signal / data / restraint-monitoring runs that all transit zone 300 — a single fire could defeat the physical separation claimed between the three dissimilar FCCs and between HV and LV routes.
praData.mitigation:
Nine-station smoke detection along hold length (SDD §5.12.2); portable extinguisher at hold access door; blade-only payload with no combustible palletised load. NO fixed hold suppression — recorded as an assumption to be substantiated.
Proposed requirements: • Substantiate the no-hold-suppression decision against §25.855 for the blade-only payload case
• Assess whether a hold fire in zone 300 can simultaneously affect FCC 2 and the HV/LV crossing points, and reflect any common cause in the FCS fault trees
aiRequirements: Substantiate the no-hold-suppression decision against §25.855 for the blade-only payload case
Assess whether a hold fire in zone 300 can simultaneously affect FCC 2 and the HV/LV crossing points, and reflect any common cause in the FCS fault trees

praData.threat: Forward equipment bay / flight-deck fire — in-flight fire or overheat in the pressurised, occupied forward zones
praData.desc: Forward equipment bay (zone 120) houses FCC 1, the two crew oxygen cylinders and forward avionics racks; the flight deck (zone 130) houses displays, inceptors, standby instrument, fire handles and crew oxygen masks. A fire in zone 120 co-locates the oxygen cylinders (an oxidiser source) with FCC 1 and avionics. No fixed suppression is described for these zones; a portable extinguisher is provided at the flight deck.
praData.csfl: FCC 1 (zone 120) is one of three dissimilar flight control computers installed in separate bays for independence; a bay fire defeats that separation for FCC 1 only. Crew oxygen cylinders in the same bay introduce an oxidiser that could aggravate a fire adjacent to FCC 1 and the forward avionics racks.
praData.mitigation:
Cylinders installed outside the flight deck and outside any zone containing a high-energy electrical source (SDD §5.13.5); thermal discharge indicator for cylinder overpressure; portable extinguisher at the flight deck; standby instrument on an independent route (SDD §5.11.5).
Proposed requirements: • Confirm crew-oxygen cylinder installation in zone 120 does not create a fire/oxidiser co-location hazard with FCC 1 and forward avionics
• Confirm the standby instrument and DC-essential feeders survive a forward-equipment-bay fire independently of the primary display feeders
aiRequirements: Confirm crew-oxygen cylinder installation in zone 120 does not create a fire/oxidiser co-location hazard with FCC 1 and forward avionics
Confirm the standby instrument and DC-essential feeders survive a forward-equipment-bay fire independently of the primary display feeders

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — unpressurised when open, pressure boundary when closed. Houses visor latches (12 rotary, common torque shaft), 8 lock pins, lock actuator, dual dissimilar sensing harness. Nose door lock sensing harness transits 110/120/130.
zsaData.equip: Visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator, proximity sensing harness, mechanical indicator linkage
zsaData.interference: Common torque shaft is a single point across all twelve latches; lock sensing harness and mechanical indicator linkage must remain separated through the bulkhead penetration; door actuation power routed opposite sensing harness — a bundle-build error could commingle them.
zsaData.mitigation: Eight independent locking pins on a separate hydraulic supply prevent latch back-drive; two dissimilar independently-routed sensing paths; pressure interlock in series with unlock command below 0.1 psi. Verify separated bulkhead penetrations at build.
housedFunctions: SF-010 Open and close nose visor
SF-011 Lock and confirm door closure

zsaData.desc: Forward equipment bay — pressurised, conditioned. Houses FCC 1, oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks. LV signal left and data network channel 1 originate here; nose door lock sensing harness transits.
zsaData.equip: FCC 1, two HP oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks, ADIRU
zsaData.interference: Oxygen cylinders co-located with avionics racks — HP gaseous oxygen adjacent to electrical energy sources; a cylinder overpressure discharge or leak bears on neighbouring equipment. FCC 1 loss removes one of three dissimilar voting channels.
zsaData.mitigation: SDD states cylinders installed 'outside any zone containing a high-energy electrical source' and supply line routed clear of HV feeder — verify at installation. Thermal discharge indicator on skin shows overboard cylinder discharge.
housedFunctions: SF-018 Acquire and present flight and navigation data

zsaData.desc: Flight deck — pressurised, occupied. Houses displays, inceptors, standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks. Nose door lock sensing harness terminates here at the mechanical indicator visible from the flight deck.
zsaData.equip: 4 display units, 2 HUDs, inceptors, integrated standby instrument, fire handles, 4 quick-donning masks
zsaData.interference: Standby instrument must share no supply/sensor/processing with primary displays — an installation error commingling feeders defeats the independent-standby claim. Fire handles and crew mask stations co-located in occupied zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Standby instrument wired directly to DC essential bus on a route independent of primary display feeders — verify routing independence at build. Reversionary display selection manual.
housedFunctions: SF-018 Acquire and present flight and navigation data

zsaData.desc: Forward hold stations 1-3 — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 1-3, restraint straps, tension monitoring loop, smoke detectors. HYD C run, HV feeder, LV signal, data channels transit; restraint tension loop runs full hold length left side.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 1-3, tension straps (2/saddle), instrumented tension loop, smoke detectors
zsaData.interference: Tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented run sharing the hold zone with the fuel gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (SDD-recorded item). Smoke detection with no suppression fitted — deliberate decision recorded as an assumption to be substantiated.
zsaData.mitigation: Two straps per saddle with neighbour load-sharing; loss of tension on two adjacent stations annunciated. Verify vent/electrical/loop separation per SDD 5.8.5. Hold no-suppression decision requires substantiation.
housedFunctions: SF-012 Restrain blade against flight/ground loads
SF-020 Detect fire and overheat (hold smoke)

zsaData.desc: Mid hold stations 4-6 — low differential, unoccupied. The crossing hub: houses saddles 4-6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points. HYD A/B wing-root run, HYD C run, HV feeder, LV signal, data channels, brake lines A/B and the ECS cross-bleed manifold all transit here.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4-6, FCC 2, mid equipment bay, HV/LV crossing points, cross-bleed manifold
zsaData.interference: Highest co-location density on the airframe. HYD A and B share the wing-root run through this zone (SDD-recorded independence item); HV and LV routes cross at the two identified points here (physical separation replaced by shielding); cross-bleed manifold joins both sides. FCC 2 is one of three dissimilar voting channels. A single zonal event here can reach multiple nominally-independent redundancies — candidate common-cause contributor to A/B and HV/LV fault trees.
zsaData.mitigation: HV/LV crossing separation maintained by shielding and defined minimum distance; A/B run separately clipped. Per ARP4761A the A/B shared run and HV/LV crossings must be reflected as common-cause contributors in the affected trees rather than left out — recommend CMA rows for both.
housedFunctions: SF-008 Provide wheel braking (brake lines A/B)

zsaData.desc: Aft hold stations 7-9 — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 7-9, aft equipment bay, FCC 3. HYD C run, LV signal, data channels and restraint tension loop transit.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 7-9, FCC 3, aft equipment bay, tension loop segment
zsaData.interference: FCC 3 loss removes the third dissimilar voting channel. Tension loop and HYD C run both transit this zone; smoke detection with no suppression continues aft.
zsaData.mitigation: Three-bay separation of FCCs (fwd/mid/aft) preserved by housing FCC 3 here separate from FCC 1 (120) and FCC 2 (300). Verify HYD C routed separately from A/B per SDD 5.4.5.
housedFunctions: SF-012 Restrain blade against flight/ground loads

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present. Houses fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route. Fuel feed gallery and wing anti-ice ducting transit.
zsaData.equip: Outboard/mid/inboard left fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice piccolo ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Flammable fluid zone with hot bleed-air anti-ice ducting and an electrical route in the same leading edge — ignition-source proximity to fuel vapour. Wing anti-ice ducting shares the leading edge with the outboard electrical route.
zsaData.mitigation: SDD states the two are separated by a shielded partition along the full run; vent/surge lines routed outboard of all electrical harnesses. Verify shielded partition integrity. Bearing PRAs: lightning, HIRF, fuel-tank ignition.
housedFunctions: SF-016 Protect airframe and inlets from ice

zsaData.desc: Right wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present (mirror of 510). Houses right fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route. Fuel gallery refuel/defuel pressure point in right wing root.
zsaData.equip: Right fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route, refuel point
zsaData.interference: Flammable fluid zone; single pressure refuel/defuel point here with overflow protection; anti-ice ducting shares leading edge with outboard electrical route.
zsaData.mitigation: Shielded partition per SDD 5.10.5; independent overflow protection circuit on refuel point. Bearing PRAs: lightning, HIRF, fuel-tank ignition.
housedFunctions: SF-016 Protect airframe and inlets from ice

zsaData.desc: Left wing root — pressure boundary transit. Houses HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit. Fuel gallery, HYD A/B run, HV feeder and bleed ducts all cross the pressure boundary here.
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder
zsaData.interference: HYD A and B share this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (SDD-recorded independence item) — a single zonal event here defeats the A/B independence claim. HV feeder and bleed duct also transit; hot bleed duct adjacent to HV feeder.
zsaData.mitigation: SDD 5.9.5: bleed duct kept clear of HV feeder with minimum separation in wing-root region; A/B separately clipped. Per ARP4761A the shared A/B run is a common-mode candidate that must appear as a common-cause contributor in A/B-dependent trees — recommend CMA row.

zsaData.desc: Right wing root — pressure boundary transit (mirror of 530). Houses HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit.
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder
zsaData.interference: Same A/B shared wing-root run crosses the pressure boundary here; bleed duct and HV feeder co-transit. Single zonal event bears on A/B independence.
zsaData.mitigation: Minimum separation of bleed duct from HV feeder per SDD 5.9.5; separately clipped A/B. Reflect A/B commonality as common-cause contributor in affected trees.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 (left outboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone. Houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing. HV feeder and bleed duct originate here.
zsaData.equip: Engine 1, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven pump, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone with high-energy rotating machinery, flammable fuel and hydraulic fluid, and electrical generation co-located. Outboard engine at 28 m moment arm — uncontained rotor burst debris trajectory bears on wing structure and opposite-side runs. Fire could reach neighbouring services in the pylon/wing root.
zsaData.mitigation: Dual-loop fire detection AND logic degrading to single-loop; two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed; fuel/hydraulic/electrical services routed through pylon, not commingled with opposite side outboard of wing root. Bearing PRAs: rotor burst (§25.903(d)(1)/AC 20-128A), engine burst (§25.901(c)), fire.
housedFunctions: SF-021 Extinguish engine and APU fire

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 2 (left inboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone. Houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing, thrust reverser. HV feeder and bleed duct transit.
zsaData.equip: Engine 2, dual-channel FADEC, generator, engine-driven pump, thrust reverser, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Fire zone; inboard engine carries thrust reverser — inadvertent in-flight deployment is a hazard bearing beyond the zone. Rotor burst debris field. High-energy/flammable co-location.
zsaData.mitigation: Reverser in-flight inhibit by WOW + radio-altimeter agreement plus mechanical translating-sleeve lock; dual-loop detection; cross-plumbed bottles. Bearing PRAs: rotor burst, engine burst, fire.
housedFunctions: SF-002 Provide reverse thrust on ground
SF-021 Extinguish engine and APU fire

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 3 (right inboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (mirror of 620). Houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, thrust reverser, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing.
zsaData.equip: Engine 3, dual-channel FADEC, generator, engine-driven pump, thrust reverser, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Fire zone; inboard engine with thrust reverser; rotor-burst debris field; high-energy/flammable co-location.
zsaData.mitigation: Reverser in-flight inhibit (WOW + radio-altimeter + mechanical lock); dual-loop detection; cross-plumbed bottles. Bearing PRAs: rotor burst, engine burst, fire.
housedFunctions: SF-002 Provide reverse thrust on ground
SF-021 Extinguish engine and APU fire

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 4 (right outboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (mirror of 610). Houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing.
zsaData.equip: Engine 4, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven pump, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Fire zone; outboard engine at 28 m moment arm — rotor-burst debris trajectory bears on wing/opposite runs; high-energy/flammable/electrical co-location.
zsaData.mitigation: Dual-loop detection AND logic; cross-plumbed bottles; pylon-routed segregated services. Bearing PRAs: rotor burst (§25.903(d)(1)/AC 20-128A), engine burst (§25.901(c)), fire.
housedFunctions: SF-021 Extinguish engine and APU fire

zsaData.desc: Left main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted. Houses three bogies, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses. Brake hydraulic lines A/B transit 710/720/300.
zsaData.equip: Three three-wheel bogies, brake lines A and B, steering actuator, brake and steering harnesses, overheat detection
zsaData.interference: Brake hydraulic lines A and B run through the bay in adjacent bundles sharing the bay (SDD-recorded zonal item) — a single bay event could take both brake supplies. Tyre burst / flailing tread within the bay bears on both lines and harnesses. Brake overheat is a fire risk in an unpressurised bay.
zsaData.mitigation: A/B bundles separately clipped and shielded; steering and braking harnesses routed on opposite sides of the bay; overheat detection fitted. Per ARP4761A the A/B brake-line co-location is a common-mode candidate for the braking trees. Bearing PRA: tire burst (PRA-54823, §25.734/AC 25.734-1).

zsaData.desc: Right main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted (mirror of 710). Houses three bogies, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses.
zsaData.equip: Three three-wheel bogies, brake lines A and B, steering actuator, brake and steering harnesses, overheat detection
zsaData.interference: Adjacent brake-line A/B bundles share the bay (SDD-recorded item); tyre burst / flailing tread bears on both lines; brake overheat fire risk.
zsaData.mitigation: Separately clipped/shielded A/B bundles; opposite-side steering/brake harness routing; overheat detection. Bearing PRA: tire burst (PRA-54823).

zsaData.desc: Nose gear bay — unpressurised. Houses nose unit, steering actuator, tow disconnect.
zsaData.equip: Twin-wheel nose unit, hydraulic steering actuator, tow mechanical disconnect
zsaData.interference: Nose-wheel tyre burst / flailing tread bears on steering actuator and adjacent harnesses; tow disconnect a potential misconfiguration source (left disconnected). Steering supply loss removes primary ground directional control.
zsaData.mitigation: Differential-braking directional control backup on loss of nose-wheel steering; mechanical disconnect for towing. Bearing PRA: tire burst (PRA-54823).

zsaData.desc: Aft fuselage and empennage — mixed environment; APU compartment is a fire zone. Houses rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders, APU compartment. Rudder control runs, LV signal and data channels transit.
zsaData.equip: Upper/lower rudder control runs, stabiliser electric heater feeders (six zones), APU, APU fire detection and bottle
zsaData.interference: APU is a fire zone adjacent to rudder control runs and stabiliser heater feeders — an APU fire bears on yaw control runs. Upper and lower rudder segment runs must remain on opposite sides; stabiliser heater feeders must stay clear of rudder runs.
zsaData.mitigation: SDD 5.10.5: stabiliser heater feeders routed opposite side of aft fuselage from rudder control runs; rudder upper/lower segment runs on opposite sides; APU dual-loop detection with automatic ground discharge. Verify separation at build. Bearing PRA: fire.
housedFunctions: SF-016 Protect airframe and inlets from ice
SF-021 Extinguish engine and APU fire

cmaData.subject: G-006 Complete loss of propulsive thrust — independence of the four per-engine thrust legs (AND)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the four engine thrust legs (per-engine FADEC, fuel supply, electrical control feed).. The four per-engine thrust legs fail independently, so complete loss requires all four to fail together.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain fuel exhaustion and total-AC-generation loss as explicit common-cause leaves under the top AND (already present as leaves 19,20). Add generator/FADEC common-design as a common-cause contributor rather than resting on the four-way AND. Substantiate cross-feed gallery isolation-valve segmentation and particular-risk/zonal coverage of the single spanwise run.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The fuel cross-feed gallery shall provide isolation such that a single gallery breach cannot deprive engines on both sides of fuel.
• Generator and FADEC common part-number/common-type susceptibility shall be evaluated for common-mode and shall not be credited as independent in the four-engine AND.
• No single AC generation-system fault shall remove control power from more than one engine.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the fuel-gallery isolation and total-AC-generation contributors appear as explicit common-cause events under the top AND, and that generator/FADEC commonality does not underpin any DAL reduction resting on this gate.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the four engine thrust legs (per-engine FADEC, fuel supply, electrical control feed).
aiRequirements: The fuel cross-feed gallery shall provide isolation such that a single gallery breach cannot deprive engines on both sides of fuel.
Generator and FADEC common part-number/common-type susceptibility shall be evaluated for common-mode and shall not be credited as independent in the four-engine AND.
No single AC generation-system fault shall remove control power from more than one engine.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm the fuel-gallery isolation and total-AC-generation contributors appear as explicit common-cause events under the top AND, and that generator/FADEC commonality does not underpin any DAL reduction resting on this gate.

cmaData.subject: G-008 Asymmetric thrust exceeding available directional-control authority (AND)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the thrust-asymmetry source (loss/rollback of engines on one side) and the yaw/directional-control authority path.. An asymmetric-thrust condition and insufficient directional-control authority are independent, so both must be present to reach the hazard.
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the electrical/command sources for engine control and for rudder actuation are segregated so no single source appears on both AND legs. Where a shared source exists, model it as a common-cause contributor across the AND rather than crediting independence.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• No single electrical or command-path fault shall both produce an engine rollback and degrade rudder/directional-control authority.
• The directional-control authority leg and the thrust-asymmetry leg of this condition shall be shown independent of common electrical generation loss.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm that the asymmetry-source leg and the directional-authority leg share no single electrical generation or command contributor, and that any shared source is represented as a common-cause event under the AND.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the thrust-asymmetry source (loss/rollback of engines on one side) and the yaw/directional-control authority path.
aiRequirements: No single electrical or command-path fault shall both produce an engine rollback and degrade rudder/directional-control authority.
The directional-control authority leg and the thrust-asymmetry leg of this condition shall be shown independent of common electrical generation loss.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm that the asymmetry-source leg and the directional-authority leg share no single electrical generation or command contributor, and that any shared source is represented as a common-cause event under the AND.

cmaData.subject: G-009 FCC issues erroneous pitch surface command surviving the vote (AND)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the flight-control-computer command generation and the voting/comparator monitor that should catch it.. An erroneous FCC pitch command and a failure of the command voting/comparator monitor are independent, so both must occur to reach the hazard.
cmaData.mitigation:
Establish and verify the software dissimilarity argument covers the comparator/monitor as well as the command function, so a common software error cannot both generate and pass the vote. Confirm the voting monitor does not share the erroneous computation or the same air-data/inertial input path as the command. Assess zone 300 zonal exposure to FCC2.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The command voting/comparator monitor shall be independent of the erroneous-command source such that a common software or data error cannot both corrupt the pitch command and defeat the monitor.
• FCC software dissimilarity shall be shown sufficient across the three voting channels to preclude a single common software error surviving the vote.
• No single zone-300 event shall simultaneously corrupt an FCC pitch command and disable the comparator monitor for that channel.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the dissimilarity argument and the monitor independence hold as implemented, and that any DAL reduction credited to the three-way vote is not invalidated by the two-team software split or FCC2 co-location.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the flight-control-computer command generation and the voting/comparator monitor that should catch it.
aiRequirements: The command voting/comparator monitor shall be independent of the erroneous-command source such that a common software or data error cannot both corrupt the pitch command and defeat the monitor.
FCC software dissimilarity shall be shown sufficient across the three voting channels to preclude a single common software error surviving the vote.
No single zone-300 event shall simultaneously corrupt an FCC pitch command and disable the comparator monitor for that channel.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm the dissimilarity argument and the monitor independence hold as implemented, and that any DAL reduction credited to the three-way vote is not invalidated by the two-team software split or FCC2 co-location.

cmaData.subject: G-011 — FCC commands pitch surface with no crew/autopilot input (AND: FCC issues uncommanded pitch command AND command voting/comparator monitor fails to inhibit)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the command-generating FCC channel and the comparator/voting monitor that inhibits an erroneous command (three dissimilar FCCs voting).. The FCC uncommanded-command failure and the command voting/comparator monitor failure are independent, so a single cause cannot both generate the erroneous command and defeat its detection.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Common software (Development/Design) — three FCCs host software from only two development teams | An error common to the two-team codebase could both produce the uncommanded command and corrupt the voting/comparator logic in the same channel set | SDD claims a dissimilarity argument but only two teams for three computers; dissimilarity between generation and monitor within a channel is not stated — independence NOT assured
Common specification / requirements error (Development/Design) | A shared requirements defect in the pitch command law would be replicated to the monitor's expected-value model, so the comparator would not flag it | Not addressed in SDD; requires evidence that monitor thresholds derive from an independent specification
Common processing / channel resource (Common Resources) — command and monitor may co-reside in one FCC | If generation and comparator share processor/data within a computer, a single processing fault defeats both | SDD does not state generation/monitor partitioning inside an FCC
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the comparator/voting monitor to be developed to an independent specification and, where hosted on the same FCC, partitioned from the command-generation function; substantiate that no single software error affects both the command law and its monitor across the two development teams.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The command voting/comparator monitor shall be functionally and specification-independent of the pitch command-generation function such that no single development or specification error can both generate an uncommanded pitch command and defeat its detection.
• The dissimilarity argument shall demonstrate that with only two development teams across three FCCs, the generation and monitor of any one channel do not share a common software or specification error.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to confirm, from the FCS software architecture and DAL P allocation, that generation and monitor are independent per the dissimilarity argument; verify against the as-built partitioning and the two-team code assignment.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the command-generating FCC channel and the comparator/voting monitor that inhibits an erroneous command (three dissimilar FCCs voting).
aiRequirements: The command voting/comparator monitor shall be functionally and specification-independent of the pitch command-generation function such that no single development or specification error can both generate an uncommanded pitch command and defeat its detection.

The dissimilarity argument shall demonstrate that with only two development teams across three FCCs, the generation and monitor of any one channel do not share a common software or specification error.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA to confirm, from the FCS software architecture and DAL P allocation, that generation and monitor are independent per the dissimilarity argument; verify against the as-built partitioning and the two-team code assignment.

cmaData.subject: G-015 — Stabiliser trim runaway to extreme (AND: erroneous/uncommanded drive to stabiliser trim AND failure to detect and arrest trim runaway)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the stabiliser trim drive (FCC command / trim actuator-motor) and the runaway detection-and-arrest monitor.. The uncommanded trim drive and the runaway detect-and-arrest function are independent, so a single cause cannot both drive the stabiliser and defeat the arrest.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Common FCC / software (Development/Design) — FCC erroneous trim output and the arrest logic may share the FCC codebase (two teams, three FCCs) | A shared FCC software or specification error could command the runaway and suppress the arrest | SDD states mechanical reversion exists to stabiliser trim but does not state that the runaway-arrest monitor is independent of the FCC trim command path — independence NOT assured
Common electrical source (Common Resources) — trim motor drive and arrest circuit power | If the arrest function and the trim drive draw from the same DC/AC feed, a supply fault could disable the arrest while the motor free-runs | EPS supplies FCCs from different sources, but the trim-drive/arrest supply split is not stated in the SDD
Shared processing of trim command and its own monitor within one FCC | Single processing fault issues the trim command and blinds the monitor | Not addressed in SDD
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the trim runaway detection-and-arrest function to be independent of the FCC trim command path (independent monitor and, where applicable, independent power feed) and to command a physical drive-disconnect; substantiate that mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim remains available after arrest.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The stabiliser trim runaway detection-and-arrest function shall be independent of the FCC trim command-generation path such that no single fault both commands a trim runaway and prevents its arrest.
• The trim runaway arrest shall command a drive disconnect independent of the electrical source powering the trim drive.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to verify, from the FCS/EPS design, that the arrest monitor and drive-disconnect are independent of the trim command path and its power feed; confirm mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim per §5.3.2 remains available.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the stabiliser trim drive (FCC command / trim actuator-motor) and the runaway detection-and-arrest monitor.
aiRequirements: The stabiliser trim runaway detection-and-arrest function shall be independent of the FCC trim command-generation path such that no single fault both commands a trim runaway and prevents its arrest.
The trim runaway arrest shall command a drive disconnect independent of the electrical source powering the trim drive.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA to verify, from the FCS/EPS design, that the arrest monitor and drive-disconnect are independent of the trim command path and its power feed; confirm mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim per §5.3.2 remains available.

cmaData.subject: G-019 — Loss of FCC command to elevator actuators (AND: FCC 1 command path lost AND FCC 2 command path lost AND FCC 3 command path lost)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators (three dissimilar computers, three separate bays, three electrical sources).. The three FCC command paths (FCC 1/2/3) to the elevator actuators fail independently, so no single cause removes all three.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Common software (Development/Design) — three FCCs, only two development teams | A software error common to the two-team codebase could remove more than one command path simultaneously | SDD dissimilarity argument mitigates but is only two-team-for-three; independence of all three paths against a common software error is not fully assured
Co-location / installation (Installation Design) — FCC 1 in zone 120, FCC 2 in zone 300, FCC 3 in zone 400 | Bays are separate, so a single-zone event does not take all three | MITIGATING — three separate bays per §5.3.5; supports the AND independence for physical events
Shared routing / EWS (Common Resources; Installation) — command paths ride the EWS routes; HV/LV cross at two points in zone 300, and FCC 2 is co-located in zone 300 with the HV/LV crossing hub | A zone-300 event (crossing point + FCC 2) could couple at least the FCC 2 path with routing serving the others | SDD identifies zone 300 as the crossing hub; the LV signal routes carry FCC command signals — routing segregation of the three command paths is a recorded item to verify
Common electrical source (Common Resources) — FCCs on three different sources; but if command paths converge on shared ACE feeds | Convergence at the actuator control electronics could couple paths | SDD states different sources per computer; ACE feed independence not stated
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators are segregated in the EWS routing (no shared route/connector/penetration, including through zone 300) and supplied from independent electrical sources; substantiate that the two-team software dissimilarity precludes a common error removing more than one path.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators shall be routed on independent EWS runs with no shared connector or penetration, including through the zone 300 crossing hub.
• The dissimilarity argument shall substantiate that no single software or specification error removes more than one of the three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to confirm, against the as-built EWS routing and the FCS software dissimilarity evidence, that the three command paths (FCC 1/2/3) share no route, connector, penetration or electrical source that would defeat the three-way AND; reconcile with the zone 300 zonal item.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators (three dissimilar computers, three separate bays, three electrical sources).
aiRequirements: The three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators shall be routed on independent EWS runs with no shared connector or penetration, including through the zone 300 crossing hub.
The dissimilarity argument shall substantiate that no single software or specification error removes more than one of the three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators.
