cmaData.subject: G-020 Loss of elevator control — AND of HYD-A elevator drive, HYD-C elevator drive, FCC command (page-1788106915833-63, gate id 49)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of HYD A vs HYD C elevator supply and of the three FCC command paths (AND-gate independence in the pitch-control tree).. The elevator is driven by two actuators on dissimilar hydraulic supplies (A and C) commanded by three dissimilar FCCs; loss of elevator control requires all legs to fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Verification phase (supports ASA/SSA). (1) HYD A and HYD C: A and B share a wing-root run at the pressure boundary (zones 530/300/540); HYD C is routed separately on the opposite side (zones 400/300/200). The A/C elevator pairing is therefore dissimilar in supply — the shared A/B run does NOT couple the elevator pair. Residual coupling: both A and C transit zone 300 (mid hold crossing hub). (2) FCC command path (gate node 56, FCC1/2/3) is a repeated dependency common to BOTH hydraulic legs — a common-cause loss of all three FCCs defeats the AND regardless of hydraulic independence. FCCs are in zones 120/300/400; FCC2 co-locates in zone 300 with HV/LV crossing points. (3) Common design: three FCCs claimed dissimilar (two dev teams, different power sources) per SDD 5.3.2 — dissimilarity is asserted, not yet verified.
cmaData.mitigation:
HYD A/C dissimilar routing and separation maintained (SDD 5.4.5). FCC dissimilarity argument (two software teams, three separate bays 5.3.5) and three independent electrical sources. Zone-300 co-location of FCC2 and HYD A/C transit to be closed by ZSA for zone 300. Mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim provides degraded pitch with all FCCs lost.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to verify: HYD A and HYD C share no reservoir/pump/routing (confirmed separate per 5.4.2); FCC1/2/3 dissimilarity (hardware, software team, power source) substantiated by DO-178C/DO-254 dissimilarity evidence; ZSA zone 300 confirms no single event takes both HYD A/C transit and FCC2.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of HYD A vs HYD C elevator supply and of the three FCC command paths (AND-gate independence in the pitch-control tree).
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA to verify: HYD A and HYD C share no reservoir/pump/routing (confirmed separate per 5.4.2); FCC1/2/3 dissimilarity (hardware, software team, power source) substantiated by DO-178C/DO-254 dissimilarity evidence; ZSA zone 300 confirms no single event takes both HYD A/C transit and FCC2.

cmaData.subject: G-021 Complete loss of pitch control authority (SF-004-TL) — AND of loss of elevator control, loss of stabiliser trim, loss of mechanical reversion (page-1788106915833-63, gate id 48)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the powered elevator/trim paths and the mechanical reversion path (top AND-gate independence, SF-004-TL).. Complete loss of pitch requires simultaneous loss of elevator control AND loss of powered stabiliser trim AND loss of mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim.
cmaData.findings: Verification phase (supports ASA). (1) The elevator sub-tree and the powered stabiliser-trim leg both depend on the three FCCs — FCC command is a repeated event across two of the three top-level AND inputs, so a common-cause FCC loss collapses both. Mechanical reversion (node 61) is the only leg NOT dependent on FCC/electrical command and is the genuine independence anchor. (2) Common design: the stabiliser trim actuator/motor and its FCC drive share the FCC dissimilarity assumption. (3) Environment: elevator actuators take HYD A and HYD C, trim is powered separately; mechanical reversion is a physical linkage independent of hydraulic pressure and of the FCCs — its independence must survive zonal/PRA exposure in the aft fuselage/empennage (zone 800) where the trim and reversion paths route.
cmaData.mitigation:
Mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim provides a survivable degraded pitch means with all three FCCs lost (SDD 5.3.2). Powered trim and elevator on separate supplies. Independence of the reversion linkage from all electrical command is the load-bearing mitigation.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to verify: the mechanical reversion linkage shares no FCC, no electrical command and no single hydraulic dependency with the powered elevator and trim; PRA (rotor burst zone 640/610, empennage) does not sever both the powered trim path and the mechanical reversion linkage; zone-800 ZSA confirms segregation of trim feeders and reversion run.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the powered elevator/trim paths and the mechanical reversion path (top AND-gate independence, SF-004-TL).
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to verify: the mechanical reversion linkage shares no FCC, no electrical command and no single hydraulic dependency with the powered elevator and trim; PRA (rotor burst zone 640/610, empennage) does not sever both the powered trim path and the mechanical reversion linkage; zone-800 ZSA confirms segregation of trim feeders and reversion run.

cmaData.subject: G-023 Loss of command to lower rudder segment — AND of loss of FBW command and loss of mechanical reversion (page-1788106915921-249, gate id 72)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the FBW command to the lower rudder segment and the mechanical reversion path to the same segment (AND-gate independence, yaw-control tree).. Loss of command to the lower rudder segment requires both the FBW command path AND the mechanical reversion path to that segment to be lost.
cmaData.findings: Verification phase (supports ASA). (1) Co-location: rudder control runs — upper and lower segment — route through the aft fuselage/empennage (zone 800). The SDD places upper and lower runs on OPPOSITE sides of the aft fuselage, but the FBW command run and the mechanical reversion run to the LOWER segment share zone 800; a zone-800 event (APU fire zone, empennage particular risk) is the credible common cause. (2) The FBW command to the lower segment (node 73) still depends on the three FCCs — same FCC common-cause exposure noted for the pitch trees. Mechanical reversion (node 74) is the independence anchor and, per SDD 5.3.2, exists to the lower rudder segment only. (3) Common environment: zone 800 mixes the APU fire zone with the rudder runs.
cmaData.mitigation:
Rudder segment runs on opposite sides of the aft fuselage (SDD 5.3.5); mechanical reversion path to lower segment independent of FBW/FCC command. Segregation of the FBW lower-segment run from the mechanical reversion run within zone 800 to be substantiated by ZSA/PRA.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to verify: the lower-segment FBW command run and the mechanical reversion linkage occupy separated positions within zone 800 with no shared penetration; PRA for the APU compartment fire zone and empennage does not sever both; the mechanical reversion path shares no FCC and no electrical command with the FBW path.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the FBW command to the lower rudder segment and the mechanical reversion path to the same segment (AND-gate independence, yaw-control tree).
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to verify: the lower-segment FBW command run and the mechanical reversion linkage occupy separated positions within zone 800 with no shared penetration; PRA for the APU compartment fire zone and empennage does not sever both; the mechanical reversion path shares no FCC and no electrical command with the FBW path.

cmaData.subject: G-025 AND independence — Complete loss of yaw control authority (SF-005-TL): upper rudder segment (HYD A + FBW) vs lower rudder segment (HYD B + FBW/mechanical reversion)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Segment segregation: upper on HYD A, lower on HYD B; rudder runs on opposite sides of aft fuselage; lower segment retains a mechanical reversion path.. The upper and lower rudder segments fail independently, each on its own actuation and its own hydraulic supply, so complete yaw loss requires both AND legs to fail.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource — the three flight control computers voting the FBW command are a shared logical source to BOTH segments; FCC 2 sits in zone 300 and all three share the FBW command architecture (common software teams under a dissimilarity argument). Installation Design — HYD A and B share a wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (zones 530/300/540); a single event on that run degrades both supplies at once, and zone 300 also carries the HV/LV crossing points and mid equipment bay (FCC 2). Environment — zone 800 houses both rudder control runs (opposite sides) plus the APU fire zone; an APU-compartment fire is a candidate common environment. Development/Design — dissimilar FCC software is a mitigating argument, not verified here.
cmaData.mitigation:
Rudder segments on opposite sides of aft fuselage; HYD A and B are separate fluid/pumping systems; three dissimilar FCCs in three separate bays; mechanical reversion to the lower segment survives total FCC loss. The A/B shared wing-root run is a recorded installation item requiring dedicated zonal attention.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The HYD A and HYD B wing-root runs shall be segregated (physical separation or protective barrier) such that no single event in zones 530/300/540 defeats both rudder segment supplies.
• The FBW command paths to the upper and lower rudder segments shall be shown independent (dissimilar computers/software and independent command routing) to substantiate the AND independence.
• A ZSA of zone 800 shall confirm no single fire/mechanical event takes both rudder control runs.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Segment segregation: upper on HYD A, lower on HYD B; rudder runs on opposite sides of aft fuselage; lower segment retains a mechanical reversion path.
aiRequirements: The HYD A and HYD B wing-root runs shall be segregated (physical separation or protective barrier) such that no single event in zones 530/300/540 defeats both rudder segment supplies.
The FBW command paths to the upper and lower rudder segments shall be shown independent (dissimilar computers/software and independent command routing) to substantiate the AND independence.
A ZSA of zone 800 shall confirm no single fire/mechanical event takes both rudder control runs.

cmaData.subject: G-028 AND independence — Slowly developing high-lift asymmetry below detection threshold (SF-006-M3): asymmetry-producing mechanism vs asymmetry protection (detect + brake)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two independent power drive units, per-section asymmetry brakes, and independent asymmetry detection annunciation.. An undetected developing asymmetry requires BOTH an asymmetry-producing mechanism AND failure of the asymmetry protection to detect/arrest it — the two AND legs are independent.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource — the two PDUs drive the high-lift surfaces through a COMMON torque shaft; a torque-shaft disconnect/distortion is a single mechanism that both defeats the two-PDU redundancy and produces the asymmetry, undermining the 'two independent PDU' basis of the producing leg. Development/Design — the asymmetry detection and the asymmetry brakes are the protection leg; if detection and brakes share sensing/actuation or a common design, a below-threshold slow build defeats both. The slow, sub-threshold rate is itself the defeater of the detection function. Common design across the two brake channels is a candidate common-cause.
cmaData.mitigation:
Two independent PDUs; asymmetry brakes at each section; independent asymmetry detection with annunciation. Common torque shaft is the recognised single element and is the reason the AND cannot be treated as fully independent.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The high-lift common torque shaft shall be substantiated as a structural/mechanical element (integrity + inspection), since it defeats the two-PDU independence relied on by the asymmetry-producing leg.
• The asymmetry detection threshold and rate coverage shall be shown to detect the slowest credible asymmetry build before it becomes hazardous.
• The asymmetry detection and asymmetry-brake channels shall be shown free of common-cause (independent sensing and actuation).
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Two independent power drive units, per-section asymmetry brakes, and independent asymmetry detection annunciation.
aiRequirements: The high-lift common torque shaft shall be substantiated as a structural/mechanical element (integrity + inspection), since it defeats the two-PDU independence relied on by the asymmetry-producing leg.
The asymmetry detection threshold and rate coverage shall be shown to detect the slowest credible asymmetry build before it becomes hazardous.
The asymmetry detection and asymmetry-brake channels shall be shown free of common-cause (independent sensing and actuation).

cmaData.subject: G-030 AND independence — Gear not in locked-down configuration at touchdown (contributor to SF-007-TL): HYD-A normal extension-to-lock vs free-fall alternate extension
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Retraction/extension by HYD system A with a free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure; downlock mechanically held, hydraulically released, with dual independent proximity sensing per unit.. Failure to reach down-and-locked requires BOTH loss of HYD-A normal extension/downlock AND failure of the free-fall alternate extension — the two means are independent.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource — HYD A is a shared resource across LDG, FCS (elevators, ailerons) and NZD; its loss is a wide common event, but the AND leg's value is that free-fall does NOT depend on HYD A. Development/Design — both normal and free-fall extension must ultimately drive the SAME downlock/uplock mechanism; a mechanical downlock fault (fails to engage/hold) is common to both AND legs and defeats the independence. Common design — the two proximity downlock circuits are 'independent' but if same-type they are a candidate common-cause for the sensing (relevant to erroneous-indication, not this FC). Installation — HYD-A extension path in the gear bays; free-fall relies on gravity + mechanical release, credible but rigging/maintenance is a common action.
cmaData.mitigation:
Free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure; mechanically held downlocks; dual independent proximity downlock sensing per unit. Shared downlock mechanism is the coupling to test.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The downlock engage/hold mechanism shall be shown not to be a common single element that defeats both HYD-A normal and free-fall alternate extension.
• The free-fall alternate extension shall be verified independent of HYD system A (no shared release actuation dependent on HYD A pressure).
• Maintenance/rigging of the downlock and free-fall release shall use segregated actions/intervals to avoid a common maintenance-induced defeat of both legs.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Retraction/extension by HYD system A with a free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure; downlock mechanically held, hydraulically released, with dual independent proximity sensing per unit.
aiRequirements: The downlock engage/hold mechanism shall be shown not to be a common single element that defeats both HYD-A normal and free-fall alternate extension.
The free-fall alternate extension shall be verified independent of HYD system A (no shared release actuation dependent on HYD A pressure).
Maintenance/rigging of the downlock and free-fall release shall use segregated actions/intervals to avoid a common maintenance-induced defeat of both legs.

cmaData.subject: G-033 — Both dissimilar lock-sensing channels falsely indicate locked (SF-010-M, page-1788106916112-987, node 95)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dissimilarity + physical separation of the two lock-confirmation channels. The proximity sensing harness (reading pin position) and the mechanical linkage / visual indicator are dissimilar and independently routed, so both cannot falsely read locked from one cause.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: proximity harness needs electrical power (backup drive/sensing/indication feed) — the mechanical indicator does not, so an electrical common cause is bounded to one channel. Installation Design / Environment: SDD routes both sensing paths in the nose door lock sensing harness through zones 110/120/130, crossing the flight-deck bulkhead at two SEPARATED penetrations; co-transit through zone 110 (visor structure, unpressurised when open) exposes both to a single zone-110 mechanical/structural event. Development/Design: channels are dissimilar in principle (proximity vs mechanical linkage) — a shared design/software error is not credible across the two. Maintenance: a common rigging/calibration action at the same station on both channels could bias both to indicate locked; not excluded by the SDD.
cmaData.mitigation:
Two dissimilar channels (proximity harness + mechanical visual indicator); routed separately from door actuation power on the opposite side of the forward fuselage; two separated bulkhead penetrations.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two lock-confirmation channels shall be physically separated within zone 110 such that no single visor-structure event disables both.
• Maintenance procedures shall prohibit a single rigging/calibration action from adjusting both lock-confirmation channels concurrently.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Dissimilarity + physical separation of the two lock-confirmation channels
aiRequirements: The two lock-confirmation channels shall be physically separated within zone 110 such that no single visor-structure event disables both.
Maintenance procedures shall prohibit a single rigging/calibration action from adjusting both lock-confirmation channels concurrently.

cmaData.subject: G-034 — Erroneous lock-engaged indication: pins not driven AND both sensing channels falsely report locked (SF-010-M, page-1788106916112-987, node 91)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the mechanical lock-engagement state and its dual-channel confirmation. The pins-not-driven branch (hydraulic/actuator fault) and the both-channels-false-locked branch fail from independent causes, so an erroneous lock-engaged indication requires two unrelated failures.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: the proximity channel and the pin actuator both draw on aircraft hydraulic/electrical supplies; loss of the lock actuator hydraulic supply can leave pins undriven while the proximity harness (if unpowered/faulted the same way) mis-reports — a shared power/hydraulic root is credible and belongs as a repeated-event contributor across the two branches. Installation Design / Environment: pins, actuator, sensing harness and mechanical linkage are ALL in zone 110 (visor structure); a single zone-110 event can both prevent full pin drive and disturb sensing — this is the dominant common-cause coupling. Development/Design: proximity vs mechanical indicator dissimilarity bounds a common sensing-design error to one confirmation channel. Maintenance: an incorrect post-maintenance pin-rig plus indicator re-zero at the same station couples both branches.
cmaData.mitigation:
Eight independent locking pins on a separate actuator and separate hydraulic supply from the visor drive; dual dissimilar sensing; pins driven through the latch bodies so latches cannot back-drive.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The lock-pin drive and both lock-confirmation channels shall not share a single hydraulic/electrical source such that its loss both prevents pin drive and falsifies confirmation.
• A repeated/common-cause event representing a zone-110 visor-structure event shall be modelled explicitly across the pins-not-driven and both-channels-false branches of gate node 91.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the mechanical lock-engagement state and its dual-channel confirmation
aiRequirements: The lock-pin drive and both lock-confirmation channels shall not share a single hydraulic/electrical source such that its loss both prevents pin drive and falsifies confirmation.
A repeated/common-cause event representing a zone-110 visor-structure event shall be modelled explicitly across the pins-not-driven and both-channels-false branches of gate node 91.

cmaData.subject: G-037 — Lock engagement lost: latch set AND locking-pin set both fail to hold (Complete loss of door lock engagement, page-1788106916157-819, node 99)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the latch set and the locking-pin set. The twelve rotary latches and the eight locking pins are independent lock elements, so loss of engagement requires both sets to fail from unrelated causes.
cmaData.findings: Development/Design (single point inside the latch branch): the twelve latches are driven by a COMMON TORQUE SHAFT — a single common-cause failure disables all twelve latches at once and is already an OR input (node 101); it does not couple to the pin set but it collapses the latch-branch redundancy and must not be treated as twelve independent latches. Common Resources: latch drive and pin actuator are on separate hydraulic supplies per the SDD, supporting independence between the two branches; however both sit in zone 110, so a single visor-structure/installation event is a credible common cause across latches AND pins — this coupling belongs as a common-cause contributor to node 99. Manufacturing: latches and pins may share a manufacturing lot / material spec; not excluded by the SDD. Installation Design: co-location in zone 110 is the governing physical common cause.
cmaData.mitigation:
Twelve latches on a common torque shaft PLUS eight pins on a separate actuator/separate hydraulic supply; pins driven through latch bodies so latches cannot back-drive while pins engaged.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• A zone-110 particular/zonal event shall be evaluated as a common cause defeating both the latch set and the locking-pin set, and represented as an explicit common-cause contributor to gate node 99.
• The common torque shaft shall be substantiated as a single latch-set failure so the latch branch is not credited as twelve-fold independent redundancy.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the latch set and the locking-pin set
aiRequirements: A zone-110 particular/zonal event shall be evaluated as a common cause defeating both the latch set and the locking-pin set, and represented as an explicit common-cause contributor to gate node 99.
The common torque shaft shall be substantiated as a single latch-set failure so the latch branch is not credited as twelve-fold independent redundancy.

cmaData.subject: G-038 — Nose door lock confirmation: proximity sensing harness vs mechanical linkage/visual indicator (both dissimilar channels)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual dissimilar lock sensing: proximity harness reads pin position directly; mechanical linkage drives a flight-deck visual indicator.. The two lock-confirmation channels are dissimilar in technology and independently routed, so both fail together only on a common cause outside the AND-gate model.
cmaData.findings: Common Environment / Installation-Design: both sensing paths transit zones 110/120/130 and both cross the flight-deck bulkhead — a zone 110 particular-risk or zonal event (visor structure) could strike both. Common Maintenance: a single rig / calibration action on the lock mechanism can mis-set both channels' reference. Mitigating independence: the channels are technologically dissimilar (electrical proximity vs mechanical/visual), share no electrical common resource, and use two separated bulkhead penetrations, so no single electrical or data resource defeats them.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm zone 110 / bulkhead-crossing separation defeats a single physical event; require independent rig procedures per channel (no shared calibration reference); reconcile against the nose-visor ZSA (zone 110) and any tire-burst / structural particular risk that reaches zone 110.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: verify installed routing separation of the proximity harness from the mechanical indicator linkage across zones 110/120/130; verify maintenance task independence; close against zone 110 ZSA.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Dual dissimilar lock sensing: proximity harness reads pin position directly; mechanical linkage drives a flight-deck visual indicator.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: verify installed routing separation of the proximity harness from the mechanical indicator linkage across zones 110/120/130; verify maintenance task independence; close against zone 110 ZSA.

cmaData.subject: G-039 — Complete loss of door lock engagement AND confirmation (top AND: engagement lost AND confirmation lost)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Twelve rotary latches on a common torque shaft + eight locking pins on a separate hydraulic supply, with dual dissimilar lock confirmation, all in series with the pressure interlock.. Lock engagement (latches + pins) and lock confirmation (dual sensing) are independent, so their simultaneous loss requires two unrelated causes.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (hydraulic): the visor/latch drive is HYD-A; the pins are on a separate supply — but a HYD-A loss coincident with a sensing fault must be examined. Common Design: the twelve latches driven by a single common torque shaft are a single-point coupling within the engagement branch (already a basic event, not a redundancy). Installation-Design / Environment: engagement hardware and both confirmation channels are co-located in zone 110 — a zone 110 particular-risk or zonal event challenges both branches of the top AND simultaneously. Ties to Catastrophic FC SF-011-TL.
cmaData.mitigation:
Surface the common torque shaft as an explicit single contributor in the engagement branch; verify HYD-A dependency does not couple engagement and confirmation; reconcile the zone 110 co-location against the nose-visor ZSA so a single zonal event is not the hidden common cause behind the top AND.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: verify no shared hydraulic/electrical resource couples the engagement and confirmation branches; verify zone 110 ZSA does not defeat the top AND; confirm common-torque-shaft treatment.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Twelve rotary latches on a common torque shaft + eight locking pins on a separate hydraulic supply, with dual dissimilar lock confirmation, all in series with the pressure interlock.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: verify no shared hydraulic/electrical resource couples the engagement and confirmation branches; verify zone 110 ZSA does not defeat the top AND; confirm common-torque-shaft treatment.

cmaData.subject: G-042 — Both tension straps at one saddle station lost (loss of longitudinal restraint at one station)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two tension straps per saddle, each tensioned by an electric winch and locked mechanically; load paths sized so a single strap loss is carried by neighbours.. The two tension straps at a station fail independently, so loss of the station requires two unrelated strap failures.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (electrical): both straps' winches consume EPS — a loss of electrical power to the station drives both winches. Common Design: the two straps and winches are identical part numbers, so a common design or manufacturing-lot defect can affect both. Common Maintenance: both straps are rigged / re-tensioned by the same crew action per turnaround, so a single installation error mis-sets both. Installation-Design / Environment: both straps and the saddle share the hold zone (200/300/400) and the same hold-floor hard point — a zonal event at the station challenges both. Ties to Catastrophic FC SF-012-PL.
cmaData.mitigation:
Add EPS-loss to a station and a common winch design/lot defect as explicit common-cause contributors; require independent rig verification per strap; note the mechanical lock provides a dissimilar hold once set, and the neighbour-station load-path sharing bounds the effect of a single station's loss; reconcile with the hold-zone ZSA.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: verify per-strap electrical feed independence at the station; verify strap/winch dissimilarity or lot control; verify independent rig-check procedure; close against hold-zone (200/300/400) ZSA.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Two tension straps per saddle, each tensioned by an electric winch and locked mechanically; load paths sized so a single strap loss is carried by neighbours.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: verify per-strap electrical feed independence at the station; verify strap/winch dissimilarity or lot control; verify independent rig-check procedure; close against hold-zone (200/300/400) ZSA.

cmaData.subject: G-045 — longitudinal strap restraint independence across nine stations (blade restraint AND gate)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Redundant dual-strap-per-station restraint with load sharing to neighbours.. The two tension straps at each of the nine saddle stations, and the stations themselves, fail independently so simultaneous loss across all stations is combinatorially remote.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (electrical): all longitudinal restraint straps are tensioned by ELECTRIC winches drawing on EPS — a single electrical-supply common cause can de-tension multiple winches simultaneously, defeating the per-station strap independence. Common Resource (monitoring): the restraint tension monitoring is a SINGLE instrumented loop over full hold length; loss of the loop removes detection of accumulating strap loss across all stations, so degradation progresses unannunciated (latent common cause on detection, not on the strap function itself). Installation/Environment: the tension monitoring loop shares the hold zone with the fuel gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (recorded item) — a zonal event in the hold (200/300/400) could strike straps and monitoring together. Manufacturing: straps/winches are of common design across stations, a common material or lot deficiency is a credible shared cause.
cmaData.mitigation:
Load paths sized so loss of any one strap is carried by neighbours (partial redundancy retained). Restraint annunciated in flight; two adjacent-station tension loss annunciated as a condition requiring immediate attention. RECOMMEND: model the shared EPS winch supply and the single monitoring loop as explicit common-cause contributors in the tree rather than relying on the pure AND; verify winch electrical segregation and monitoring-loop coverage.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The winch electrical supplies for the nine restraint stations shall be segregated such that no single electrical source loss de-tensions more than one station.
• The restraint tension monitoring shall provide coverage such that undetected loss over any strap is bounded and annunciated.
cmaData.status: Development/verification deficiency identified — independence not assured on shared electrical supply and single monitoring loop
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Redundant dual-strap-per-station restraint with load sharing to neighbours.
aiRequirements: The winch electrical supplies for the nine restraint stations shall be segregated such that no single electrical source loss de-tensions more than one station.
The restraint tension monitoring shall provide coverage such that undetected loss over any strap is bounded and annunciated.

cmaData.subject: G-046 — combined longitudinal AND geometric restraint independence (blade restraint AND gate)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Longitudinal restraint by straps AND lateral/vertical restraint by saddle geometry, both on nine saddles pinned to hold-floor hard points.. Loss of longitudinal strap restraint and loss of geometric (saddle) restraint are independent, so complete restraint loss requires both branches to fail together.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (structure): both the strap load paths and the geometric saddle restraint terminate at the SAME hold-floor hard points — 'There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points.' A single hard-point / floor-beam structural failure is a common cause that defeats BOTH branches simultaneously, so the AND is not genuinely independent (this is why the sibling common-hard-point branch exists in the parent OR). Common Resource (electrical): longitudinal winch tensioning shares EPS (as G-045); geometric restraint is passive saddle geometry, so this coupling is one-sided (strap branch only). Installation/Environment: all nine saddles and both restraint mechanisms are co-located in the hold zones (200/300/400) — a single zonal event (impact, fire) can strike both branches at a station.
cmaData.mitigation:
Geometric (lateral/vertical) restraint is passive and shares no electrical supply with the winches, giving genuine dissimilarity of MEANS between the two branches. Structural common cause is captured at the parent OR gate via the dedicated common-hard-point branch (per FTA structure). RECOMMEND: retain the common-hard-point failure as an explicit contributor (repeated event) and substantiate hard-point integrity by structural analysis and Particular Risk Analysis — the hard points are structure, not a functional-FHA item.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The hold-floor hard points shall be substantiated against a single-failure common-cause defeat of both longitudinal and geometric restraint by structural analysis and Particular Risk Analysis.
cmaData.status: Common-cause structural coupling identified — hold-floor hard points defeat the two branches jointly; substantiate by structural/PRA
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Longitudinal restraint by straps AND lateral/vertical restraint by saddle geometry, both on nine saddles pinned to hold-floor hard points.
aiRequirements: The hold-floor hard points shall be substantiated against a single-failure common-cause defeat of both longitudinal and geometric restraint by structural analysis and Particular Risk Analysis.

cmaData.subject: G-049 — in-flight reverse-thrust deploy inhibit independence (WOW/RA agreement inhibit AND mechanical sleeve lock)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two dissimilar in-flight deploy inhibits: an electronic WOW + radio-altimeter agreement interlock AND a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.. The WOW/radio-altimeter agreement inhibit and the mechanical translating-sleeve lock fail independently, so inadvertent in-flight deployment requires both inhibits defeated together.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (data/sensor): the WOW discrete is a SINGLE weight-on-wheels source distributed to a large number of consumers (reversers, pressurisation, restraint monitor, configuration). An erroneous WOW 'on-ground' discrete is a shared cause that defeats the WOW-agreement inhibit for BOTH inboard reversers simultaneously — coupling the two per-engine G-049 instances to each other, and reducing the electronic inhibit to effectively a single point. Development/Design: dual inboard reversers share common control design and common inhibit logic — a specification or software error in the inhibit logic is a common cause across both. Common Resource (electrical): reverser control electronics and inhibit logic draw on EPS. The two inhibits within one engine (electronic vs mechanical) are DISSIMILAR in means, which supports the AND for a single engine; the residual concern is the cross-engine common cause via shared WOW and common logic.
cmaData.mitigation:
The two inhibits are dissimilar in nature (electronic agreement + independent mechanical sleeve lock), which is genuine within-engine independence. Radio-altimeter agreement is required in addition to WOW, providing a second dissimilar 'in-flight' input so a single erroneous WOW alone does not defeat the electronic inhibit. RECOMMEND: confirm the radio-altimeter channel used for the agreement is independent of the WOW source and not itself a shared point across both reversers; model shared WOW as an explicit common-cause contributor if the RA independence cannot be substantiated.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The in-flight deploy inhibit shall not be defeated by any single erroneous weight-on-wheels indication, and the radio-altimeter agreement source shall be independent of that indication.
• The reverse-thrust inhibit logic shall be substantiated against a common specification/software error defeating the inhibit on both inboard reversers.
cmaData.status: Within-engine independence supported by dissimilarity; cross-engine WOW/logic common cause to be substantiated
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Two dissimilar in-flight deploy inhibits: an electronic WOW + radio-altimeter agreement interlock AND a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.
aiRequirements: The in-flight deploy inhibit shall not be defeated by any single erroneous weight-on-wheels indication, and the radio-altimeter agreement source shall be independent of that indication.
The reverse-thrust inhibit logic shall be substantiated against a common specification/software error defeating the inhibit on both inboard reversers.

cmaData.subject: G-052 — In-flight deploy inhibits fail (both defeated), inboard reverser
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dissimilarity of inhibit means: an electronic agreement vote and a mechanical translating-sleeve lock fail from unrelated causes.. The two in-flight deploy inhibits (WOW/radio-altimeter agreement AND mechanical translating-sleeve lock) are independent, so both must fail for an in-flight deployment.
cmaData.findings: The two inhibits are genuinely dissimilar in kind (electronic agreement vote vs mechanical lock), which supports the AND. Residual concerns: the WOW discrete and radio-altimeter data are sourced from LDG (SF-007) and AVI (SF-018) respectively and consumed widely; erroneous WOW-in-air-shows-ground could satisfy the electronic side without an independent fault. Common design/software of the reverser control produces the uncommanded-deploy command that the inhibits must catch. Both inhibit paths and the actuation sit in the same nacelle fire zone (620/630), a shared harsh/high-energy environment.
cmaData.mitigation: Dissimilar inhibit means retained; WOW derived from multiple gear units with cross-check; radio-altimeter dual (two radio altimeters per SDD); mechanical sleeve lock independent of electrical power. Verify WOW/RA agreement monitor is not defeated by a single erroneous source.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Dissimilarity of inhibit means: an electronic agreement vote and a mechanical translating-sleeve lock fail from unrelated causes.

cmaData.subject: G-050 — Inadvertent deployment — inboard reverser (one unit)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Per-unit independence: the deploy-command path and the inhibit set for one reverser fail independently, and this unit is independent of the second inboard unit.. An inadvertent deployment of one inboard reverser requires an uncommanded deploy command/actuation AND both in-flight inhibits defeated, treated independently of the other inboard unit.
cmaData.findings: Within the unit the AND holds only if the inhibit set (G-052) is genuinely independent of the deploy-command path — the reverser control produces both the uncommanded command and, if erroneous, could bias the WOW/RA-fed inhibit logic (common controller/software concern). Across units, both inboard reversers (zones 620, 630) share reverser control design, FADEC channel design and the same in-flight inhibit logic — a common design/software contributor that the OR-of-two-units structure does not capture. Both nacelles are identical-build fire zones (high energy, flammable fluid).
cmaData.mitigation: Mechanical translating-sleeve lock independent of the control/actuation electronics provides a dissimilar second barrier. Verify reverser control and inhibit monitor do not share a processing lane. Assess common design/software across the two inboard units as a dedicated common-cause contributor to the OR of the two units.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Per-unit independence: the deploy-command path and the inhibit set for one reverser fail independently, and this unit is independent of the second inboard unit.

cmaData.subject: G-053 — Inadvertent deployment — other inboard reverser (one unit)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Per-unit independence mirrored: the second inboard reverser's deploy-command path and inhibit set fail independently, and independently of the first unit.. An inadvertent deployment of the second inboard reverser requires an uncommanded deploy command/actuation AND both in-flight inhibits defeated, treated independently of the first inboard unit.
cmaData.findings: Mirror of G-050. The per-unit AND is supported by the dissimilar mechanical sleeve lock. Cross-unit independence between G-050 and G-053 is the weaker claim: both units share reverser control design, FADEC channel design and identical in-flight inhibit logic (common design/software), and both are installed in identical-build nacelle fire zones (620/630) — a shared harsh environment. A common design error or common erroneous WOW/RA source could bias both units' inhibit logic together, which the independent OR of the two units understates.
cmaData.mitigation: Dissimilar mechanical sleeve lock per unit retained. Verify the WOW/RA inhibit source is not a single common feed to both inboard reversers, and add a common-design/common-software contributor covering both inboard reverser control channels rather than relying on the independent per-unit ANDs alone.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Per-unit independence mirrored: the second inboard reverser's deploy-command path and inhibit set fail independently, and independently of the first unit.

cmaData.subject: G-055 — Aileron hydraulic drive independence (HYD B AND HYD C)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of HYD B (engine-driven, eng 3&4) and HYD C (AC electric-motor pumps + RAT) supplies to the aileron actuators — separate fluid, pumping and distribution.. Ailerons retain roll authority because they are driven by two actuators on independent hydraulic systems B and C; simultaneous loss of both is an AND.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (electrical): HYD C normal pumping is by AC electric motor pumps — a total loss of AC generation removes HYD C's normal source, leaving only RAT; HYD B is unaffected, so AC loss degrades but does not by itself defeat the pair. Common Resource (electrical/EWS): both aileron actuators' control electronics draw on the EPS/EWS spine; if the two actuator command feeds are not on segregated sources/routes the hydraulic independence is undercut at the electrical layer — SDD does not state actuator-electronics routing. Installation: SDD records A and B (not B and C) as the shared wing-root run, so the recorded wing-root co-location does NOT strike this B/C pair. Environment: aileron actuator co-location at the wing has not been characterised in the SDD.
cmaData.mitigation:
Systems A, B and C entirely separate in fluid, pumping and distribution (§5.4.2); RAT backstop preserves HYD C on total AC loss; A/B (not B/C) share the wing-root run so this pair avoids that co-location.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The aileron HYD-B and HYD-C actuator command electronics shall be supplied from segregated electrical sources and routed on physically separated paths such that no single EPS/EWS event disables both.
• The installation shall substantiate that the HYD-B and HYD-C aileron actuators do not share a zone or routing that a single particular risk (rotor burst, tyre burst, fire) could sever together.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm as-installed segregation of the two aileron actuator supplies and command electronics, and to confirm RAT availability logic preserves HYD C on total AC generation loss; ZSA/PRA to confirm no single-zone/single-routing common cut at the aileron actuator installation.
cmaData.status: Open — actuator command-electronics segregation and aileron actuator co-location not substantiated in SDD
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of HYD B (engine-driven, eng 3&4) and HYD C (AC electric-motor pumps + RAT) supplies to the aileron actuators — separate fluid, pumping and distribution.
aiRequirements: The aileron HYD-B and HYD-C actuator command electronics shall be supplied from segregated electrical sources and routed on physically separated paths such that no single EPS/EWS event disables both.
The installation shall substantiate that the HYD-B and HYD-C aileron actuators do not share a zone or routing that a single particular risk (rotor burst, tyre burst, fire) could sever together.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm as-installed segregation of the two aileron actuator supplies and command electronics, and to confirm RAT availability logic preserves HYD C on total AC generation loss; ZSA/PRA to confirm no single-zone/single-routing common cut at the aileron actuator installation.

cmaData.subject: G-056 — FCC command independence to aileron actuators (FCC 1 AND FCC 2 AND FCC 3)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three FCC command paths to the aileron actuators — three dissimilar computers, three separate bays, three different electrical sources, two-team dissimilar software.. Aileron control survives because three dissimilar flight control computers vote on command; loss of all three command paths is an AND of three.
cmaData.findings: Development/Design (software): SDD hosts FCC software from one of two teams under a dissimilarity argument — three computers but only two software builds, so a latent common software/specification/tool error can affect the two channels sharing a build; the dissimilarity argument is the independence hypothesis that must be tested, not assumed. Common Resource (data): the FCC command is carried on a dual-redundant deterministic data network; a network-level common mode (protocol/timing/common network stack) could corrupt command to multiple channels. Installation Design (co-location): FCC 1 in zone 120, FCC 2 in zone 300 (the HV/LV crossing hub, with HYD A/B, brake lines and cross-bleed manifold transiting), FCC 3 in zone 400 — three separate bays satisfy physical separation; a zone-300 event strikes only FCC 2. Common Resource (electrical): three different electrical sources claimed; if two share an upstream bus/source that commonality would erode the three-way independence — not substantiated at bus level in the SDD.
cmaData.mitigation:
Three dissimilar FCCs on three different electrical sources in three separate bays (§5.3.2/§5.3.5); two-team dissimilar software; network channels on opposite sides sharing no connector or penetration (§5.11.5); mechanical reversion path exists to lower rudder and stabiliser trim (but NOT to ailerons).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two-team software dissimilarity argument shall be substantiated to show no single specification, requirement or tool error can simultaneously corrupt the aileron command output of more than one FCC channel.
• The three FCC aileron-command paths shall be shown to derive from three electrically independent sources with no shared upstream bus that a single fault could remove.
• Data-network common-mode failures (protocol, timing, common stack) shall be shown not to corrupt aileron command across multiple FCC channels simultaneously.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to close the dissimilarity claim against the two-build software architecture, confirm three-way electrical-source segregation, and confirm the deterministic network cannot present a common corrupted command to multiple channels; ZSA to confirm no two FCC bays share a zone/routing.
cmaData.status: Open — two-build software dissimilarity coverage and FCC electrical-source segregation at bus level not substantiated
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three FCC command paths to the aileron actuators — three dissimilar computers, three separate bays, three different electrical sources, two-team dissimilar software.
aiRequirements: The two-team software dissimilarity argument shall be substantiated to show no single specification, requirement or tool error can simultaneously corrupt the aileron command output of more than one FCC channel.
The three FCC aileron-command paths shall be shown to derive from three electrically independent sources with no shared upstream bus that a single fault could remove.
Data-network common-mode failures (protocol, timing, common stack) shall be shown not to corrupt aileron command across multiple FCC channels simultaneously.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to close the dissimilarity claim against the two-build software architecture, confirm three-way electrical-source segregation, and confirm the deterministic network cannot present a common corrupted command to multiple channels; ZSA to confirm no two FCC bays share a zone/routing.

cmaData.subject: G-058 — FCC command independence to roll spoilers (FCC 1 AND FCC 2 AND FCC 3)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three FCC command paths to the roll spoiler actuators — three dissimilar computers, three separate bays, three different electrical sources, two-team dissimilar software.. Roll spoiler authority survives because three dissimilar flight control computers vote on command; loss of all three command paths is an AND of three.
cmaData.findings: Development/Design (software): as G-056, three computers hosting only two software builds under a dissimilarity argument — a latent common software/specification/tool error can affect the two channels sharing a build; the roll-spoiler command shares this same FCC set, so the software common mode is identical to the aileron path and is NOT an independent second layer against a common FCC-software fault. Common Resource (data): roll spoiler command rides the same dual-redundant deterministic data network; a network common mode is shared with the aileron path. Installation Design: FCC 1 (zone 120), FCC 2 (zone 300 crossing hub), FCC 3 (zone 400) — separate bays; a single zonal event strikes only one channel. Cross-effect: because ailerons AND roll spoilers both depend on the same three FCCs, a common FCC-software or FCC-network fault is a common cause across G-056 and G-058 together, eroding the roll-axis redundancy that pairs ailerons with spoilers.
cmaData.mitigation:
Three dissimilar FCCs in three separate bays on three different electrical sources (§5.3.2/§5.3.5); network channels on opposite sides sharing no connector or penetration (§5.11.5).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two-team software dissimilarity argument shall be substantiated to show no single specification/requirement/tool error can simultaneously corrupt roll-spoiler command across more than one FCC channel.
• The independence between the aileron and roll-spoiler roll paths shall be substantiated against common FCC-software and common data-network faults, since both depend on the same three FCC set.
• The three FCC roll-spoiler command paths shall be shown to derive from three electrically independent sources with no shared upstream bus.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to close the dissimilarity and network common-mode claims for the roll-spoiler command paths and to confirm that a common FCC fault cannot remove both aileron and roll-spoiler roll authority together.
cmaData.status: Open — shared FCC software/network common mode across aileron and spoiler roll paths not bounded
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three FCC command paths to the roll spoiler actuators — three dissimilar computers, three separate bays, three different electrical sources, two-team dissimilar software.
aiRequirements: The two-team software dissimilarity argument shall be substantiated to show no single specification/requirement/tool error can simultaneously corrupt roll-spoiler command across more than one FCC channel.
The independence between the aileron and roll-spoiler roll paths shall be substantiated against common FCC-software and common data-network faults, since both depend on the same three FCC set.
The three FCC roll-spoiler command paths shall be shown to derive from three electrically independent sources with no shared upstream bus.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to close the dissimilarity and network common-mode claims for the roll-spoiler command paths and to confirm that a common FCC fault cannot remove both aileron and roll-spoiler roll authority together.

cmaData.subject: G-060 roll-control AND independence — HYD supply independence (aileron/spoiler)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent hydraulic supply to redundant roll effectors. Aileron authority (HYD B+C) and spoiler authority (HYD B) are lost only by independent hydraulic failures
cmaData.findings: HYD B is a shared resource across both the aileron path (B+C) and the spoiler path (B); a single HYD B loss removes spoiler roll authority and one aileron actuator supply. HYD A and B additionally share a wing-root run crossing the pressure boundary at zones 530/300/540 (recorded installation item), a candidate installation/environment common cause. HYD C is routed separately along the opposite side.
cmaData.mitigation:
Ailerons retain drive from HYD C when B is lost; spoilers are supplementary roll effectors with ailerons primary. Confirm zonal separation of the A/B wing-root run adequately protects HYD B, or model HYD B as a repeated event / common-cause contributor across the roll-effector branches.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS shall retain sufficient roll control authority with any single hydraulic system (A, B or C) lost, per the outboard-engine-out sizing case.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: confirm the A/B shared wing-root run does not defeat HYD B independence claimed at node 148; verify roll authority with HYD B lost against the sizing case.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independent hydraulic supply to redundant roll effectors
aiRequirements: The FCS shall retain sufficient roll control authority with any single hydraulic system (A, B or C) lost, per the outboard-engine-out sizing case.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: confirm the A/B shared wing-root run does not defeat HYD B independence claimed at node 148; verify roll authority with HYD B lost against the sizing case.

cmaData.subject: G-060 roll-control AND independence — three-FCC vote independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three dissimilar flight control computers. The three flight control computers fail independently so the command-path AND (nodes 151/158) holds
cmaData.findings: FCC 2 is installed in the mid equipment bay, zone 300 — the crossing hub where HV/LV crossing points, HYD A/B run, HYD C run, brake lines and the ECS cross-bleed manifold all transit. A zone-300 event (fire, HV/LV cross, overheat) is a candidate installation/environment common cause against FCC 2, but FCC 1 (zone 120) and FCC 3 (zone 400) are in separate bays. Software is dissimilar across two teams (common-design mitigation). EPS is the common resource, mitigated by three different electrical sources.
cmaData.mitigation:
Three separate bays (120/300/400) provide physical separation; dissimilar software mitigates common-mode software error; three different electrical sources mitigate common power. Substantiate that no single zone-300 event takes more than FCC 2.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The three flight control computers shall be installed such that no single zonal event affects more than one computer.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: verify bay separation (120/300/400) and dissimilar-software argument close the three-way vote independence; confirm zone-300 co-location of FCC 2 does not couple to FCC 1/3.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three dissimilar flight control computers
aiRequirements: The three flight control computers shall be installed such that no single zonal event affects more than one computer.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: verify bay separation (120/300/400) and dissimilar-software argument close the three-way vote independence; confirm zone-300 co-location of FCC 2 does not couple to FCC 1/3.

cmaData.subject: G-061 FADEC engine-1 dual-channel AND independence — common design/software
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the dual redundant FADEC channels. FADEC channel A and channel B must both fail to issue an uncommanded thrust command
cmaData.findings: The two channels are a common FADEC design cross-linked to the opposite channel for data only; a common specification/software/hardware design error is a candidate common cause defeating the channel AND. Power feeds are independent per §5.1.2, mitigating the common-resource path.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independent power feeds; cross-link is data-only. Assess the common-design/software error path — dual channels of one design do not protect against a systematic command error; a monitor or dissimilarity argument may be required.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The engine control shall detect and inhibit an uncommanded thrust command arising from a common design or software error affecting both FADEC channels.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: substantiate the DAL and dissimilarity/monitoring argument for the dual-channel FADEC common-design path (DO-178C/DO-254 as applicable).
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the dual redundant FADEC channels
aiRequirements: The engine control shall detect and inhibit an uncommanded thrust command arising from a common design or software error affecting both FADEC channels.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: substantiate the DAL and dissimilarity/monitoring argument for the dual-channel FADEC common-design path (DO-178C/DO-254 as applicable).

cmaData.subject: G-061 FADEC engine-1 dual-channel AND independence — common nacelle environment
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Environmental independence of the dual FADEC channels. FADEC channel A and channel B are not disabled by a single shared environment
cmaData.findings: Both channels are installed within engine nacelle 1 (zone 610), a high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone. A nacelle fire, overheat, or uncontained rotor/engine-burst debris is a candidate common environment defeating the channel AND. Reconcile with the applicable rotor-burst (§25.903(d)(1)/AC 20-128A) and engine-burst (§25.901(c)) particular risks and the nacelle zonal analysis.
cmaData.mitigation:
Dual-loop fire detection and extinguishing in the nacelle (SF-020/SF-021). Substantiate via PRA/ZSA that a single nacelle event is bounded to loss of the one engine and does not couple across the two channels in a way that produces an uncommanded (as opposed to loss-of-thrust) output.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: cross-reference nacelle PRA (rotor/engine burst) and zone-610 ZSA to confirm the shared-nacelle environment does not defeat the dual-channel independence at node 165.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Environmental independence of the dual FADEC channels
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: cross-reference nacelle PRA (rotor/engine burst) and zone-610 ZSA to confirm the shared-nacelle environment does not defeat the dual-channel independence at node 165.

cmaData.subject: G-065 — FADEC dual-channel independence, engine 3 (SF-001-M)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual redundant FADEC channels with independent power feeds, cross-linked for data only, fail independently.. FADEC channel A and channel B fail independently so that an uncommanded thrust command requires both channels to fail (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source | Effect on Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence :: (1) Common FADEC hardware/software design across both channels | a design or software error defeats both channels simultaneously | engine model not yet released to engineering, so channel dissimilarity is UNKNOWN and cannot be credited — dominant common-cause contributor. (2) Cross-channel data link | erroneous shared datum propagates to both channels | SDD limits the link to 'data only', but a corrupt datum can still bias both channels — logical common cause. (3) Co-location in nacelle zone 630 (fire zone, high energy, flammable fluid) | a thermal/mechanical/EMI event in the nacelle strikes both channels | both channels housed in the same engine, no zonal separation between them. (4) Common manufacturing lot / common part number across the four engine positions | latent lot defect present in both channels | staggered overhaul not stated for FADEC; commonality recorded as item to examine. (5) Common maintenance/calibration action on both channels | a single erroneous maintenance action corrupts both | no dissimilar-maintenance provision stated.
cmaData.mitigation: Establish and substantiate FADEC channel dissimilarity (hardware and/or software) once the engine model is released; treat the cross-channel data link as a monitored, comparison-protected path; confirm nacelle installation does not couple channels beyond the shared engine; apply lot-diversity or staggered-overhaul controls; require dissimilar or independently-verified maintenance actions per channel.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Dual redundant FADEC channels with independent power feeds, cross-linked for data only, fail independently.

cmaData.mitigation:
Dual-loop fire detection and extinguishing in the nacelle (SF-020/SF-021). Substantiate via PRA/ZSA that a single nacelle-2 event is bounded and does not couple across the two channels into an uncommanded output.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: cross-reference nacelle PRA (rotor/engine burst) and zone-620 ZSA to confirm the shared-nacelle environment does not defeat dual-channel independence at node 171.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Environmental independence of the dual FADEC channels
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: cross-reference nacelle PRA (rotor/engine burst) and zone-620 ZSA to confirm the shared-nacelle environment does not defeat dual-channel independence at node 171.

acReqData.text: The aircraft shall limit the probability of complete loss of propulsive thrust to less than 1e-9 per flight hour.

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew cannot arrest the developing yaw with the rudder authority available, so no crew recovery of directional control is credited for this asymmetric-thrust condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-001-PL2 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew cannot recover propulsive thrust, so a forced descent and off-field landing with no thrust is not credited as a survivable crew recovery at most phases.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-001-TL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the sudden asymmetry and configuration change, identifies it as an inadvertent in-flight reverse-thrust deployment, and applies corrective control to retain the reduced control margin.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-002-M · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the unstowed reverser during rollout, identifies the resulting directional-control demand, and applies increased steering and control input to maintain track.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-002-M2 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the absence of expected reverse thrust during rollout, identifies the reduced deceleration, and reassesses the stopping margin to apply the appropriate braking response.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-002-M3 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew perceives the reduced deceleration from the deceleration cues, identifies the partial reverse-thrust shortfall, and modulates braking or autobrake to hold the stopping margin.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-002-PL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew recognises the absence of reverse thrust, identifies the reduced deceleration against the surface condition, and applies maximum available wheel braking to stop within distance.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-002-TL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the discrepancy between the commanded roll and the aircraft's actual roll response, identifies it as an erroneous roll response, and applies corrective input to hold the intended flight path.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-003-M · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the uncommanded roll from the attitude indication, identifies it as an uncommanded roll motion, and applies corrective roll input to arrest the excursion.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-003-M2 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the jammed roll surface from the degraded roll response, identifies the reduced or asymmetric roll authority, and flies the intended path using the remaining roll means and any required trim or offset.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-003-M3 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew is unaware of the developing roll bias and does not identify its source, taking no corrective action until the lateral deviation becomes perceptible.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-003-M5 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the annunciated roll degradation, identifies the reduced roll capability, and flies the degraded configuration while observing the applicable restrictions.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-003-PL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the degraded roll response, identifies the loss of lateral flight-path capability, and applies sustained corrective input to maintain the lateral path in demanding cases.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-003-PL2 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew perceives the incorrect pitch response to their command, diagnoses it as an erroneous pitch response, and applies a countering input without compounding the error.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-M · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the uncommanded pitch motion from the attitude and pitch-rate indication, identifies the source, and applies corrective pitch input to arrest it.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-M2 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the large sustained out-of-trim force and reduced pitch authority, identifies the jam or trim runaway, and counters it using the remaining pitch means or the mechanical reversion path to the stabiliser trim.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-M3 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew does not perceive the slow uncommanded pitch or flight-path change below the detection threshold and takes no corrective action until the deviation becomes apparent.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-M4 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew does not detect the slow trim runaway below the detection threshold and takes no corrective action until the accumulated mistrim manifests as a control-force or attitude change.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-M5 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the annunciated degraded pitch law, identifies the reduced pitch authority, and applies increased control effort to maintain flight path and speed.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-PL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the directional bias from the jammed rudder segment, identifies the degraded directional handling, and holds heading and trims out the bias with the remaining yaw means.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-M3 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew is unaware of the uncommanded yaw developing below the detection threshold and takes no corrective action.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-M4 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew is unaware of the slowly developing steady yaw bias and takes no corrective action.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-M5 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the reduced yaw response, identifies the partial loss of directional control authority, and applies increased rudder and control input to maintain directional control, particularly in the engine-out or crosswind case.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-PL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the reduced yaw response, identifies the partial loss of directional control authority, and applies maximum available directional input, which is not credited to maintain control in the engine-out sizing case.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-PL2 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew cannot arrest the yaw or sideslip by any available means, so no crew recovery of directional control is credited for the complete loss of yaw control authority.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-TL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the unexpected configuration change and asymmetry, identifies the uncommanded high-lift movement, and applies corrective control to counter it.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-006-M · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the erroneous high-lift position via annunciation, identifies the actual configuration, and reverts to it and adjusts the speed schedule accordingly.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-006-M2 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew is unaware of the slowly developing high-lift asymmetry below the detection threshold and takes no corrective action until the resulting roll becomes apparent.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-006-M3 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the degraded high-lift deployment, identifies the reduced configuration, and applies the degraded-configuration procedure with revised approach speeds.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-006-PL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the annunciated high-lift asymmetry, identifies the restrained-configuration case, and applies lateral trim to fly a restricted-configuration approach per procedure.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-006-PL2 · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew detects the loss of high-lift capability, identifies the non-standard high-speed configuration, and flies the revised approach while managing landing-distance margin at the semi-prepared strip.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-006-TL · framed per ARP4761A §3.10 crew-procedure assumption
